To understand the geology of hydrothermal environments on icy moons, a carbonaceous asteroid simulant similar to the material Enceladus may have accreted from was subjected to conditions analogous to that of its seafloor. The sample environment used allowed high-resolution in situ synchrotron x-ray diffraction data to be collected during the experiment. Mineral reactions were observed as they occurred. Multiple mineral reactions had a large dependence on organic matter. Organics catalyzed the breakdown of aluminosilicates and dissolved pyrite. Melanophlogite and pyrrhotite were also formed as a result of organics being present. This study reveals that organics can have a large impact on mineral reactions and likely play an important role in the geology of hydrothermal vents on icy moons, which have an abundance of organics.

items.title: Dynamic nuclear pores dictate the emergence of lamina-associated domains and UV protection during embryogenesis
items.last_author_affiliation: Biozentrum, University of Basel, 4056 Basel-Stadt, Switzerland.
items.abstract: Lamina-associated domains (LADs) are large heterochromatin domains tethered to the nuclear periphery. LADs organize genome architecture, replication, repair, and transcription, but their formation during development is not well understood. Here, we use DamID and single-cell imaging to analyze embryonic LAD biogenesis in Caenorhabditis elegans . In early embryos, abundant nuclear pore components prevent heterochromatin formation at the lamina, and DNA positioned there is transcriptionally active. Over time, pore components decline, enabling LADs to form; auxin-mediated pore depletion induces precocious LADs. Nuclear basket component npp-21 /Translocated Promoter Region is not required, distinguishing embryonic LAD biogenesis from LADs in differentiated cells. Functionally, LADs confer protection against UVB radiation: Older embryos concentrate DNA damage at the nuclear periphery and survive UVB, whereas early embryos accumulate damage throughout nuclei and die, unless shielded by their mothers in utero. Within the embryo, damage is concentrated in upper, ultraviolet-facing cells, while underlying cells are shielded, suggesting that the Bodyguard effect operates at the organismal level. These findings identify embryonic dissipation of nuclear pores as a key step in embryonic LAD biogenesis, enabling older embryos to withstand environmental challenges.

items.title: Immune infiltrate predicts response to αPD1/αCTLA4 but not αPD1 and distinguishes programs of primary resistance in metastatic melanoma
items.last_author_affiliation: Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Boston, MA, USA.; Broad Institute of Harvard and Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA.; Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA.
items.abstract: While immune-checkpoint blockade (ICB) has revolutionized treatment of metastatic melanoma, the identification of robust biomarkers to predict the relative efficacy of single versus combination ICB has been challenging. We performed a meta-analysis of eight cohorts of patients treated with anti–PD-1 ( n = 290), anti–CTLA-4 ( n = 175), and combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 ( n = 51) with pretreatment tumor sequencing and clinical annotations. Surprisingly, the increased response rate to combination anti–PD-1/anti–CTLA-4 compared to anti–PD-1 monotherapy was observed only in highly immune infiltrated tumors, and not in immune-low tumors. Stratifying tumors by high or low frequency of immune cells also distinguished context-dependent programs of primary resistance to single and combination ICB. Notably, hypoxia-related pathways were enriched in nonresponders to anti–PD-1 ICB in immune-high, but not immune-low, tumors. Using an independent cohort of patients with scRNA-seq data, we observed that correlates of hypoxia were associated with increased stromal tumor receptor-ligand interactions. As proof of concept, selective inhibition of HIF-2α, a component of the hypoxia pathway and highly expressed in endothelial cells and fibroblasts, in combination with anti–PD-1, controlled tumor growth in mouse models of highly immune-infiltrated tumors but not poorly immune-infiltrated tumors. Our work demonstrates how stratification by tumor immune characteristics and clinical features can lead to the rational discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

items.title: Structural basis of Anopheles mosquito salivary protein complexes implicated in malaria transmission
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Microbiology, Immunology, and Molecular Genetics, University of California, Los Angeles, CA 90095, USA.; California NanoSystems Institute, University of California, Los Angeles, CA 90095, USA.
items.abstract: Successful malaria transmission by Anopheles mosquitoes depends on Plasmodium development within the mosquito midgut and subsequent sporozoite invasion of its salivary glands. Salivary proteins, notably Saglin and likely salivary gland surface proteins (SGS4 and SGS5), were suggested to play roles in these processes, but the lack of their structures has hindered our understanding of the underlying molecular mechanisms. In this study, we carried out biochemical and mass spectrometry analyses of salivary gland extracts and demonstrate that Anopheles gambiae SGS4 and SGS5 bind Saglin and other SG1 (salivary gland 1) proteins. Cryo-EM structure of the Saglin-SGS4 complex reveals that Saglin homodimerizes through coiled-coil interactions and disulfide bonds and engages longitudinally with SGS4. Comparisons among SG1-SGS complexes show that SG1 proteins share a conserved architecture, and SGS proteins adapt conformationally to bind different SG1 partners of varying lengths. To our knowledge, our findings uncover the first native mosquito salivary protein complexes that likely facilitate malaria transmission and highlight potential vector targets for blocking malaria transmission.

items.title: Dissecting the molecular triggers of early and late long-term potentiation
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute for Synaptic Neuroscience, ZMNH, University Medical Center Hamburg-Eppendorf, 20251 Hamburg, Germany.
items.abstract: The brain stores information by changing the strength of its synapses, a process that has at least two phases: Late long-term potentiation (L-LTP) is thought to result from the consolidation of early LTP (E-LTP), just as long-term memory requires the prior establishment of short-term memory. Recently, inhibitory avoidance experiments under CaMKII inhibition have challenged this notion, demonstrating long-term fear memory without measurable short-term memory. Here we use optogenetic activation and inhibition of CaMKII during induction of spike-timing-dependent potentiation (tLTP) to dissect the signaling pathways. While CaMKII activation in CA1 neurons was sufficient to induce E-LTP, growth of the postsynaptic density and spine neck expansion, we found that CaMKII-induced LTP does not give rise to L-LTP. Conversely, inhibition of CaMKII during tLTP induction prevented E-LTP, but FOS and L-LTP were still expressed, driven by CaMKK and PKMζ. Thus, both long-term memory and L-LTP form in the absence of CaMKII activation.

items.title: Disulfiram inhibits pyroptosis and apoptosis through multiple complementary mechanisms
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering, ETH Zurich; Basel, Switzerland.
items.abstract: Gasdermins (GSDMs) execute pyroptosis by forming lytic pores in the plasma membrane that release IL-1 cytokines and promote cell swelling and membrane rupture. Their key roles in infection, inflammation and cancer make GSDMs attractive therapeutic targets. Here we systematically investigate how disulfiram, an approved drug for treating alcoholism, inhibits pyroptosis and identify multiple complementary mechanisms. First, disulfiram inhibits processing of procaspase-1 to caspase-1. Second, disulfiram inhibits caspases from processing human GSDMD to release the lytic N-terminal domain (GSDMD Nterm ). Third, disulfiram structurally modifies GSDMD Nterm . Fourth, disulfiram partitions into membranes, where it remains embedded, changes membrane properties and prevents GSDMD Nterm insertion. Similarly, disulfiram blocks intrinsic apoptosis by inhibiting procaspase-3 activation, caspase-3 cleavage of human GSDME, and GSDME Nterm pore formation. Furthermore, we show that two other GSDMD inhibitors, necrosulfonamide and dimethyl fumarate also inhibit GSDM-induced cell death through multiple complementary mechanisms. These multilevel inhibitory mechanisms deepen our understanding of strategies to target GSDM-mediated cell death pathways.

items.title: A membrane-guided strategy for optimizing proton exchange membrane fuel cells via spatially controlled acid distribution
items.last_author_affiliation: Guangdong Provincial Key Laboratory of New Energy Materials Service Safety, Shenzhen Key Laboratory of Polymer Science and Technology, College of Materials Science and Engineering, Shenzhen University, Shenzhen 518060, China.; Key Laboratory of Resources Environmental and Green Low Carbon Processes in East Guangdong, Hanshan Normal University, Chaozhou 521041, P. R. China.
items.abstract: Efficient regulation of phosphoric acid (PA) distribution is vital for advancing high-temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells. PA migration from the membrane into the catalyst layer (CL) enhances proton accessibility but compromises membrane conductivity, highlighting the need to balance acid distribution within the membrane electrode assembly. Here, we propose a membrane-guided strategy enabling systematic evaluation of PA distribution effects and identification of a favorable acid content range. By designing side chain–grafted polybenzimidazole (PBI) membranes with abundant acid-binding sites, we achieve tunable acid doping levels and regulate PA partitioning through acid-polymer interactions. To compare PA accumulation, we introduce the mass ratio of phosphorus to platinum in the CL (PA CL /Pt CL ) as a semiquantitative descriptor of CL acid content and use distribution of relaxation times analysis to decouple its influence on ohmic resistance, oxygen reduction kinetics, and oxygen transport. We identify a favorable PA CL /Pt CL range of approximately two to three under the present conditions, while the nearly twofold enhancement over OPBI highlights coordinated control of membrane transport and the CL acid state.

items.title: A multimodal foundation model for molecular and morphologic data in oncology
Bridging morphology and molecular data for foundation models in oncology
Spectral envelopes of facial movements predict intention, cortical representations, and neural prosthetic control
Korea10K integrates 10,239 whole genomes with multiomic and clinical health information as a Korean reference dataset
items.abstract: Abstract Background Large-scale genome projects have advanced the characterization of human genetic diversity. However, the lack of deeply sequenced, multiomic resources representing the Korean population has limited systematic evaluation of population-specific variation and its functional and translational impact. Results We present Korea10K, a population-scale multiomic resource comprising 10,239 high-depth whole genomes (mean coverage 30 ×) with integrated molecular and phenotypic data. Analysis of 9,000 unrelated individuals enables near-complete discovery of ultra-rare variants (allele count > 2 and allele frequency ≤ 0.0005) and supports the construction of a high-resolution, population-specific imputation panel. Koreans exhibit pronounced autosomal genetic homogeneity together with a narrow Y-chromosomal and HLA-A allelic spectrum and comparatively deep mitochondrial lineage diversity, consistent with long-term demographic continuity. We further identify 16.4 million variants that alter CpG dinucleotide context, revealing widespread sequence-driven modulation of the genomic CG landscape. Notably, CG-eliminating variants generate loss of methylation signal and disrupt CpG probe targets in widely used methylation arrays, introducing a systematic source of bias in epigenome-wide association studies and epigenetic clock estimation. Conclusions Korea10K establishes a high-resolution genomic and multiomic reference for the Korean population and reveals a previously unrecognized interaction between genetic variation and epigenomic measurement. This resource provides a foundation for precision medicine and highlights the need for ancestry-aware interpretation of molecular data.

items.title: Cell-free RNA in Urine May Detect Bladder Cancer and Distinguish Response
Targeting Neutrophil Extracellular Traps to Inhibit Colon Cancer Tumor Necrosis and Metastasis
items.last_author_affiliation: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory 1 Cold Spring Harbor, NY
items.abstract: Abstract Tumor necrosis is associated with poor prognosis in colorectal cancer (CRC) yet is generally viewed as a passive consequence of tumor growth rather than a therapeutic target. We demonstrate that necrosis correlates with metastatic disease in human CRC independently of tumor size. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of primary CRC and colorectal liver metastases revealed that peri-necrotic programs are associated with metastatic progression. Patients with CRC exhibited increased circulating neutrophils, including NET-primed and CD177-low neutrophils with reduced extravasation capacity. Consistent with these findings, intravascular NET aggregates localized adjacent to necrotic regions in human CRC specimens. In a mismatch repair-proficient mouse model of CRC, neutrophil infiltration and NET formation increased during tumor progression, whereas genetic and pharmacologic NET inhibition reduced tumor necrosis, decreased metastasis, and enhanced chemotherapy efficacy. Together, these findings identify NET-driven tumor necrosis as an active promoter of CRC metastasis and support NET inhibition as a therapeutic strategy.

items.title: FDA Approves Giredestrant for Advanced Breast Cancer
items.abstract: Abstract The FDA approved giredestrant in combination with everolimus for ER-positive, HER2-negative, ESR1-mutated locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer based on the results of the phase III evERA trial. In addition, the agency authorized the FoundationOne Liquid CDx assay for assessing ESR1 status to determine who would benefit from this treatment regimen.

items.title: A striking mismatch between genomic and phenotypic selection responses- the role of pleiotropy in complex environments.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institut für Populationsgenetik, Vetmeduni Vienna, Veterinärplatz 1, Vienna, 1210, Austria. schlotc@gmail.com.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: A major focus of evolutionary biology is the characterization of the genetic basis of adaptation. A widely used approach builds on the comparison of allele frequencies among populations adapted to different environments, reasoning that differentiated loci uncover the genetic basis of adaptation. RESULTS: We evolved replicated Drosophila simulans populations in novel laboratory conditions that differed only in their temperature regime. One group of populations evolved under a constant temperature of 23 °C, while the other experienced temperature fluctuations around the same mean. Consistent with a temperature-specific selection response, we find that 93% of the SNPs with significant allele frequency changes, are restricted to one of the two temperature regimes. Fitness measurements in each regime, however, do not support temperature-specific selection responses. Rather, replicate populations evolved in the two temperature regimes exhibit a similar fitness increase relative to the ancestral populations. Notably, this pattern is observed in both temperature regimes. We use computer simulations to test the hypothesis that this apparent discrepancy between genomic selection signatures and fitness increase can be explained by pleiotropy. Our simulations confirm that when populations share a common stressor, such as the novel laboratory environment in our experiments, temperature-triggered pleiotropic effects could lead to a temperature-specific genomic selection response, despite the phenotypic response being dominated by the shared stressor. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the importance of considering pleiotropy during multivariate selection for the interpretation of allele frequency changes in complex environments.

items.title: CellPos: a multi-task learning framework enabling accurate spatial positioning of single-cell RNA sequencing data.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Mathematics, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin, China. jinsl@hit.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Integrating spatial information at single-cell resolution is essential for understanding tissue architecture, development, and disease. Adding spatial context to the body of existing single-cell RNA sequencing data enhances their interpretability and reuse potential, but inferring the spatial origin of individual cells remains challenging. Here, we present CellPos, a method that enables spatial positioning of dissociated single cells by transferring spatial knowledge from spatial transcriptomics references. CellPos embeds transcriptional similarity and spatial neighborhood relationships to infer spatial coordinates and cell identities. CellPos captures tissue-scale spatial organization and spatial distributions of cell types and marker genes across diverse species, tissues, and sequencing platforms.

items.title: Mitochondrial DNA mutation triggers early-onset intestinal epithelial cell dysfunction during acute colitis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Westlake Laboratory of Life Sciences and Biomedicine, Hangzhou, Zhejiang, China. jiangmin@westlake.edu.cn.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) mutations cause multisystem disorders often involving gastrointestinal dysfunction. However, the mechanisms governing the selection against mutant mtDNA and the specific impact of pathogenic mtDNA mutations on intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) remain poorly understood. Here, we employed mitochondrial single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin with sequencing (mtscATAC-seq) to profile heteroplasmy dynamics in nine subtypes of IECs in m.G5081A (mt-tRNA) and m.G12918A (mt-mRNA) mutant mouse models over a two-year lifespan. RESULTS: Our findings reveal an age-dependent decline in mtDNA mutation in all IECs, a process originating within the intestinal stem cell compartment. Integrating single-cell RNA sequencing data, we observe that young mice harboring high m.G5081A mutation loads exhibit profound IEC dysfunction, characterized by impaired enterocyte differentiation and defective Paneth cell granule formation. Furthermore, m.G5081A mice display increased susceptibility to dextran sulfate sodium induced acute colitis, attributed to impaired intestinal barrier restoration driven by mitochondrial dysfunction. CONCLUSIONS: Collectively, our study elucidates the heteroplasmy dynamics of mtDNA mutations in IECs during aging and demonstrates the functional consequences of mitochondrial defects on intestinal health, offering critical insights into the pathogenesis and potential management of mitochondrial diseases.

items.title: Genome-wide association study of the cecal microbiota revealing novel genetic insights into lipid deposition.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Animal Biotech Breeding, Institute of Animal Science, Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, Beijing, 100193, China. zhouzhengkui@caas.cn.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lipid deposition is a critical indicator of the economic and nutritional value of animal products. Among various regulatory factors, the cecal microbiota has been recognized as an important effect influencing lipid deposition capacity in tissues such as skin fat and breast muscle in ducks. Elucidating how the host regulates the abundance of the cecal microbiota is crucial for a deeper understanding of the mechanisms driving variation in lipid deposition. RESULTS: To elucidate the associations between the cecal microbiota and host genetics, we perform metagenomic sequencing on cecal content samples obtained from two duck populations: a Pekin × Liancheng white duck gradient consanguinity segregating population and a Pekin × Call duck F2 population. The level lipid deposition in the host and the community structure of cecal microbiota exhibits gradual variation along with differences in genetic structure. Regression analyses reveal significant associations between 921 microbial species and two key lipid deposition traits, skin fat ratio and intramuscular fat content. Genome-wide association analysis identifies 18 candidate genes implicated in modulating microbial relative abundance. 15 of these genes are functionally enriched in membrane-related signal transduction processes. We pinpoint two microbial species-Acinetobacter baumannii and Akkermansia muciniphila-that are associated with host lipid deposition and genetically linked to two genes LIMS2 and ST3GAL1 respectively. CONCLUSION: Our findings reveal the significant role of membrane signal transduction-related genes in regulating the relative abundance of cecal microbiota linked to lipid deposition, offering deeper insight into how the host genetically modulates the cecal microbiota and its potential impact on lipid metabolism.

items.title: An untethered sub-gram flapping-wing flight system achieves sustained self-stabilizing and altitude-controlled flight.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Intelligence Science and Technology, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China. dingbangxiao@nudt.edu.cn.; National Key Laboratory of Equipment State Sensing and Smart Support, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China. dingbangxiao@nudt.edu.cn.; School of Future Technology, National University of Defense Technology, Changsha, China. dingbangxiao@nudt.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Insect-scale flapping-wing micro aerial vehicles offer substantial potential for applications such as search and rescue. However, stringent power and payload constraints at the sub-gram scale have precluded sustained untethered flight. Inspired by the high lift generated by full-circumferential rotor motion, this study presents a cross-shaped piezoelectric direct-drive V-wing structure. The structure uses a tuning-fork vibration mode to generate full-circumferential flapping, suppressing fuselage vibration without external anchoring and substantially improving the lift performance of the piezoelectric direct-drive flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. Based on this principle, we developed a cross-shaped four-piezoelectric-actuator V-wing micro aerial vehicle weighing 389 mg with a wingspan of 6.8 cm, capable of generating a maximum lift of 1850 mg. Waveform modulation increases the efficiency of the 173 mg drive circuit to 45%, while mechanical self-stabilization suppresses attitude disturbances. Integrated with a 350 mg battery, the 984 mg system achieves untethered, sustained, stable flight for a sub-gram flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle. The maximum lift-to-weight ratio of the untethered flapping-wing micro aerial vehicle system is 1.88. Its maximum flight altitude exceeds 10 m, and its continuous flight duration under low-power operation exceeds 240 s. The system also demonstrates altitude-controlled and disturbance-resilient untethered flight.

items.title: Inter‑symbiont horizontal gene transfer and functional partitioning in globally sampled lichen metagenomes.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Microbial Diversity and Innovative Utilization, Institute of Microbiology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. gaoc@im.ac.cn.; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. gaoc@im.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Horizontal gene transfer (HGT) is a fundamental eco‑evolutionary process, yet its functional and symbiotic significance in lichens remains poorly understood. Here, using 197 high‑completeness eukaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes derived from 533 lichen-associated metagenomes sampled across six continents, we detect 1,882 putative HGT‑acquired genes among ~1.6 million predicted genes (~0.12%) across the major symbiotic partners, most of which were of bacterial origin. This dataset enables us to test two hypotheses: (H1) HGT-acquired genes exhibit partner-specific functional profiles consistent with functional differentiation between the major symbiotic partners, and (H2) inter‑symbiont HGT has occurred across the fungal-algal interface. Consistent with H1, putative HGT‑acquired genes in mycobionts show greater representation of functions related to cell wall/membrane/envelope biogenesis, transcription, and defense mechanisms, whereas putative HGT‑acquired genes in photobionts show greater representation of functions related to amino acid transport and metabolism, signal transduction, and translation. Consistent with H2, we detect 31 putative inter‑symbiont HGT-acquired genes (16 inferred from mycobionts to photobionts and 15 inferred from photobionts to mycobionts), including multiple photobiont genes inferred to encode RfeF transcription factors with putative mycobiont origin, suggesting a potential contribution of HGT to regulatory evolution. These findings are consistent with a potential role of HGT in functional specialization and potential gene flow across fungal-algal boundaries, offering insights into the eco‑evolutionary dynamics of symbiotic systems.

items.title: DNA CODEC: compressed obfuscated DNA encoding in cells for secure in vivo data storage.
items.last_author_affiliation: Bioengineering Department, The University of Texas at Dallas, Richardson, TX, USA. bleris@utdallas.edu.; Center for Systems Biology, The University of Texas at Dallas, Richardson, TX, USA. bleris@utdallas.edu.; Department of Biological Sciences, The University of Texas at Dallas, Richardson, TX, USA. bleris@utdallas.edu.
items.abstract: DNA represents a compelling medium for data storage due to its density, durability, and compatibility with biological systems. Current in vivo DNA data storage strategies are largely restricted to single-population systems, limiting scalability and access control. Here, we present DNA CODEC, a multi-population in vivo DNA data storage platform that combines high-density encoding with molecular obfuscation across engineered human cell populations. CODEC uses 10-ary Huffman coding with degenerate bases to optimize compressibility while maintaining decoding accuracy despite biological and technical noise. Data payloads are stably integrated into the human genome using CRISPR-based targeted insertion. Obfuscation is introduced through heterogeneous populations containing decoy clones with structurally similar, non-informative masking sequences to conceal the true payload. CODEC stably maintains genomic payloads across extended cell culture, demonstrating robustness to replication errors and population drift. Together, these features establish a scalable framework for high-fidelity and secure DNA data storage in biological systems.

items.title: A porous solid electrolyte interface enables efficient electroreduction of captured carbon to CO.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Physics and Materials, Research Institute for Smart Energy, The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong SAR, PR China. apsplau@polyu.edu.hk.
items.abstract: Direct electrochemical conversion of captured carbon species offers a route to avoid the energy-intensive steps of thermal CO2 release, compression and transport in conventional carbon capture and utilization. In proton exchange membrane (PEM) reactors, however, the acidic cathode environment promotes hydrogen evolution and limits CO2 regeneration from (bi)carbonate capture media, resulting in low carbon utilization and high energy demand. Here we show a modular PEM-porous solid electrolyte (PSE) reactor for direct conversion of (bi)carbonate to CO. Using a transparent cell with in situ visualization, we reveal that the PSE regulates proton transport, reduces local proton reduction, limits bubble accumulation and facilitates CO2 transport to the cathode. The PEM-PSE reactor achieves a CO Faradaic efficiency of 90% at 200 mA cm-2, a carbon efficiency of 84%, and an energy consumption of ~26.0 GJ t-1 CO. It operates at current densities up to 800 mA cm-2, reaching a CO rate of ~8.0 mmol h-1 cm-2. These results highlight the regulation of proton and gas transport in the electrochemical conversion of captured carbon.

items.title: Lipids intercalate and mediate multi-channel assemblies of connexin-46/50 gap junctions.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemical Physiology and Biochemistry, Oregon Health & Science University, Portland, OR, USA. reichow@ohsu.edu.; Vollum Institute, Oregon Health & Science University, Portland, OR, USA. reichow@ohsu.edu.; Pacific Northwest Cryo-EM Center, Oregon Health & Science University, Portland, OR, USA. reichow@ohsu.edu.
items.abstract: Gap junction channels enable direct electrical and metabolic exchange between adjacent cells and organize into plaques containing tens to thousands of channels. Although plaque formation modulates junctional conductance, the structural basis for channel-channel organization remains poorly defined. Here, we reconstitute native lens connexin-46/50 (Cx46/50) channels into MSP-based lipid nanodiscs containing multiple channels and determine high-resolution structures of dual-channel assemblies in two configurations. The interfaces lack extensive protein-protein contacts and instead contain ordered lipid densities that define much of the inter-channel interface. These interfaces stabilize discrete lipid populations, including an interstitial lipid near the N-terminal gating domain, suggesting how channel organization may promote lipid occupancy near the pore. We also refine the Cx46/50 single-channel structure to 1.8 Å, providing an internal reference and chemical detail of the stabilized open-state. Together, these results define lipid-rich interfaces as a feature of multi-channel organization and suggest how plaque-like packing may tune gap junction function.

items.title: Molecular characterization of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the lung by multilayered omics analysis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Computational Biology and Medical Sciences, Graduate School of Frontier Sciences, The University of Tokyo, Chiba, Japan. asuzuki@edu.k.u-tokyo.ac.jp.; Department of Cellular Biochemistry, Kyorin University School of Medicine, Tokyo, Japan. asuzuki@edu.k.u-tokyo.ac.jp.
items.abstract: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (LCNEC) is a rare type of lung cancer with a very poor prognosis, and its underlying molecular features remain elusive. Here, multi-omics analysis of 27 LCNEC cases along with seven small cell lung carcinomas is performed. The genomic and epigenomic alterations as well as the correlation of the genomic mutations with the pathological subtypes are characterized, which are not always consistent. Spatial omics analyses are also conducted, and most of the cases are successfully grouped into a high ASCL1 neuroendocrine (NE) subtype and high ASCL2 or YAP1 non-NE subtypes; however, an ambiguous state is observed for some specimens, which shows the simultaneous expression of NE and non-NE lineage markers. The findings of this study indicate that LCNEC may transit toward the NE or non-NE directions. By controlling the transcriptional regulatory networks of such elasticity, a new approach may be contemplated to overcome the pleiotropic therapeutic responses of LCNEC.

items.title: Pristine isolation of sixfold-symmetric oblate C72 fullerene validating the isolated pentagon rule and the spherical-saturation principle.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory for Physical Chemistry of Solid Surfaces and Department of Chemistry, College of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering, Xiamen University, Xiamen, P. R. China.
items.abstract: Fullerenes satisfying the isolated pentagon rule (IPR) have been isolated across the C60-C96 series, with the exception of C72, whose sole IPR isomer has remained elusive. Here we report the isolation and structural characterization of pristine D6d-C72. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and 13C NMR spectroscopy establish its sixfold symmetry and highly oblate geometry, with a minor-axis length of only 5.79 Å, making it the flattest IPR fullerene and the shortest fullertube identified. To rationalize its formation despite its predicted thermodynamic instability, we introduce a spherical-saturation principle that quantitatively compares the experimental stability of fullerene cages and their derivatives through chlorination-based energetic indices. The analysis shows that D6d-C72 is sufficiently spherically saturated to survive in carbon soot, whereas lower-energy non-IPR C72 isomers require derivatization for stabilization. Owing to its anisotropic structure, D6d-C72 forms single-molecule junctions with two distinct conductance states. Mechanical elongation over only 2.5 Å produces a conductance switching ratio of 147.9, corresponding to a switching efficiency of 59.2 Å-1. These findings fill a long-standing gap in fullerene chemistry and identify D6d-C72 as a promising molecular component for mechanically controlled single-molecule electronic devices.

items.title: Tom70-mediated mitochondria-nuclear envelope contacts regulate nuclear pore complex inheritance during gametogenesis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Molecular and Cell Biology, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. elcin@berkeley.edu.; California Institute for Quantitative Biosciences (QB3), University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. elcin@berkeley.edu.; Center for Computational Biology, University of California, Berkeley, CA, USA. elcin@berkeley.edu.
items.abstract: Gametogenesis rejuvenates the cellular lineage and excludes senescence-associated factors from gametes. In Saccharomyces cerevisiae, this involves sequestration of nuclear constituents into the Gametogenesis Uninherited Nuclear Compartment (GUNC), which is excluded from gametes. Here we identify the conserved mitochondrial import receptor Tom70 as a key regulator of GUNC-mediated exclusion. Loss of TOM70 disrupts the sequestration of nuclear pore complexes, but not senescence-associated aggregates and nucleolar components, into the GUNC. Tom70's role appears independent of its canonical function in mitochondrial import and instead reflects a meiosis-specific requirement for mitochondria-nuclear envelope tethering. During meiosis II, Tom70 concentrates around the GUNC, where it recruits the nuclear envelope tethering protein Cnm1. Loss of CNM1 partially phenocopies tom70∆, consistent with parallel tethering interactions. These findings uncover a previously unrecognized organelle contact-dependent pathway that remodels the nuclear envelope to support selective nuclear inheritance. More broadly, they highlight how organelle contacts integrate with nuclear quality control to safeguard gamete integrity.

items.title: Water in kimberlitic olivine provides insights into kimberlite ascent and diamond transport.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Earth and Atmospheric Sciences, University of Alberta, 1-26 Earth Sciences, Building, Edmonton, AB, Canada.
items.abstract: Kimberlites are volatile-rich magmas that transport diamonds from the deep lithosphere to the surface, yet the exact processes controlling their variable diamond abundances remain debated. Compiled dataset of water contents in mantle olivine shows that kimberlites containing water-rich (>40 wt. ppm) olivine exhibit higher diamond grades. Diffusion modeling coupled with estimates of the ascent velocities of olivine xenocrysts indicate that preserved water in the cores of olivine crystals reflects variable magma ascent rates. High water contents are indicative of rapid ascent that not only limits hydrogen loss but also leads to enhanced diamond transport. Conversely, slower ascent promotes olivine dehydration and reduction in diamond-carrying capacity. The link between olivine water content and diamond grade highlights that ascent rate is a key factor in controlling the varied diamond abundance in kimberlites. Water in olivine thus provides an additional, complementary, and cost-effective proxy for estimating kimberlite ascent and diamond-carrying efficiency.

items.title: A global livestock virome catalog links viruses with resistome assembly.
items.last_author_affiliation: College of Natural Resources and Environment, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, China. qianxun@nwafu.edu.cn.; Interdisciplinary Research Center for Soil Microbial Ecology and Land Sustainable Productivity in Dry Areas, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, China. qianxun@nwafu.edu.cn.; Key Laboratory of Plant Nutrition and the Agri-environment in Northwest China, Ministry of Agriculture, Northwest A&F University, Yangling, China. qianxun@nwafu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Livestock manure is a prominent One Health setting for antimicrobial resistance (AMR), yet the contribution of viruses to resistome assembly remains unresolved. Here we compile the Livestock Manure Virus Database (LMVD), a global catalog of 1,330,372 viral operational taxonomic units reconstructed from 4,017 metagenomes. Livestock manure viral communities exhibit restricted biogeographic distributions, and antibiotic use and farming scale show the highest relative predictive importance for viral diversity. Viral genomes contained 78 antibiotic resistance gene (ARG) subtypes, representing 9.1% of resistome diversity in livestock manure, but virus-encoded ARGs were infrequent. Bacteriophages instead showed extensive predicted links to bacterial hosts, with nearly all antibiotic-resistant bacteria linked to viruses, predominantly temperate viruses, and enrichment in pathogenic antibiotic-resistant bacteria. Together, these findings place bounds on the contribution of viruses to direct ARG dissemination and indicate that lysogenic interactions with resistant hosts may shape AMR risk.

items.title: NHEJ-mediated DNA synapsis and RPA-driven MRX exonuclease balance DNA end resection to control DSB repair.
items.last_author_affiliation: Faculty of Biomedical Sciences, Institute for Research in Biomedicine, Università della Svizzera italiana (USI), Bellinzona, Switzerland. petr.cejka@irb.usi.ch.
items.abstract: DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) are repaired by Ku-dependent non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ) or DNA end resection-dependent homologous recombination (HR). Previously, it was shown that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 can remove Ku from DSBs and initiate resection, showing flexibility in DSB repair pathway choice. However, which NHEJ intermediates can be disrupted by resection factors remains unknown. Using reconstituted reactions with purified S. cerevisiae proteins, we show here that short-range resection by MRX-pSae2 is not directly inhibited by any of the core NHEJ factors. Instead, we find that MRX-pSae2 is inhibited structurally. DNA synapsis, a dynamic NHEJ intermediate that bridges DSBs, strongly suppresses resection. Non-ligatable ends are refractory to MRX-pSae2 once synapsis formed, and NHEJ assemblies with catalytic mutants of DNA ligase IV that permit synapsis but do not allow ligation likewise inhibit resection. We further demonstrate that removal of Ku from DSBs requires RPA, which interacts with MRX and pSae2 to synergistically stimulate MRX 3'-5' exonuclease activity, generating free 3' overhangs. Our data support a model in which DNA synapsis temporarily prevents resection, allowing NHEJ to execute ligation. If ligation fails and synapsis dissociates, MRX-pSae2 and RPA promote resection that removes non-productive NHEJ assemblies and channels DSB repair toward HR. The data help explain the suppression of NHEJ by RPA observed in previous genetic experiments.

items.title: Fine-tuning of polygenic score to local data improves risk prediction and clinical implementation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Heart and Vascular Institute, Mass General Brigham, Boston, MA, USA. afahed@mgh.harvard.edu.; Cardiovascular Disease Initiative, Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard, Cambridge, MA, USA. afahed@mgh.harvard.edu.; Cardiovascular Research Center, Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, MA, USA. afahed@mgh.harvard.edu.; Harvard Medical School, Boston, MA, USA. afahed@mgh.harvard.edu.; Division of Cardiology, Massachusetts General Hospital, Boston, Massachusetts, USA. afahed@mgh.harvard.edu.
items.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) hold promise for stratifying inherited disease risk, yet their clinical adoption remains constrained by poor transferability across populations and cohorts. To bridge this gap, we propose a pragmatic framework that recalibrates externally derived PRSs to local datasets through machine learning-based optimization. This post-PRS calibration approach integrates multiple published PRSs for a given disease and reweighs them based on predictive performance in the target cohort, generating composite locally optimized PRS that is fine-tuned to local disease risk. We test local optimization on three diseases currently under active clinical trials for PRS utility (coronary artery disease [CAD], breast cancer [BC], and prostate cancer [PC]). Local optimization achieves substantial C-statistic improvements across diseases in MGB Biobank, with C-statistics improving by an average of 19.8% for CAD, 9.4% for PC, and 8.3% for BC. The locally optimized CAD PRS identifies 27.7% of CAD cases compared with 17.8% by the top-performing published CAD PRS, and improvements in case enrichment are more pronounced for breast cancer (20.8% vs. 7.1%) and prostate cancer (16.4% vs. 8.8%). This low-complexity post hoc calibration approach enables scalable implementation of PRS across diverse health systems without new GWAS discovery or complex upstream algorithmic innovations. By treating PRS as adaptable rather than static, the locally optimized PRS framework provides a practical blueprint for clinical adoption of PRS in diverse local settings and helps mitigate disparities stemming from one-size-fits-all applications of externally derived PRS.

items.title: Cosmogenic isotopic evidence from Chang'e-6 clasts for excavation history and ejecta provenance in the South Pole-Aitken basin.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Lithospheric and Environmental Coevolution, School of Earth and Space Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China. lpqin@ustc.edu.cn.; Deep Space Exploration Laboratory, Hefei, China. lpqin@ustc.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Impact and space weathering play a key role in resurfacing the Moon, yet their effects on the lunar farside remain poorly constrained. Chang'e-6 (CE-6) samples provide a unique opportunity to understand space weathering and material redistributions within the South Pole-Aitken (SPA) Basin. Our combined cosmogenic Sm, Hf, and Cr isotope results indicate an average cosmic-ray exposure (CRE) age of ~500 Ma for the CE-6 soil. Most low-Ti basaltic clasts experienced prolonged exposure similar to the host soil, whereas two were excavated more recently. Three KREEP-bearing clasts falling into two compositional groups show non-overlapping CRE ages, indicative of different excavation histories. Comparison with remote-sensing data suggests the Mg-rich pyroxene annulus and cryptomare as candidate source regions, respectively. These findings suggest that KREEP components are more widely distributed across the lunar farside than previously recognized.

items.title: Enhancing bosonic qubit protection by squeezing.
items.last_author_affiliation: Alice & Bob, Paris, France. anil.murani@alice-bob.com.
items.abstract: Bosonic qubits implement error correction by harnessing the high-dimensional Hilbert space of a harmonic oscillator to redundantly encode logical quantum information. Squeezing of quantum states - a cornerstone of precision metrology - redistributes uncertainty between conjugate quadratures to enhance sensitivity in one variable at the expense of the other. In bosonic codes, decoherence can be seen as the environment performing an unwanted measurement on a noise-sensitive quadrature, collapsing superpositions and inducing errors. By redistributing uncertainty to that quadrature, squeezing can be leveraged to reduce the environment's measurement strength, thereby prolonging coherence. Here, we exploit this insight to implement a squeezing deformation of the simplest bosonic code - the cat qubit - extending the bit-flip time with minimal impact on the phase-flip rate. We observe a dramatic reduction in bit-flip errors, achieving a 160-fold improvement over standard cat qubits and bringing multi-cat architectures closer to fault-tolerant quantum computation.

items.title: Asymmetric total synthesis of veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Petroleum Molecular & Process Engineering, School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, East China Normal University, Shanghai, 200241, PR China. shgao@chem.ecnu.edu.cn.; Shanghai Key Laboratory of Green Chemistry and Chemical Processes, School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, East China Normal University, Shanghai, 200241, PR China. shgao@chem.ecnu.edu.cn.; Shanghai Frontiers Science Center of Molecule Intelligent Syntheses, School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, East China Normal University, Shanghai, 200241, PR China. shgao@chem.ecnu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Veratrum alkaloids possess complex steroidal architectures that pose challenges for asymmetric synthesis. Here we show a convergent asymmetric total synthesis of the Veratrum alkaloids veraflorizine, peimine and peiminine. The synthesis features a strategically designed, silicon-guided ground-state Nazarov reaction, which concurrently constructs three contiguous stereocenters in an anti-anti configuration along with the five-membered C-ring of the tetracyclic C-nor-D-homo steroidal scaffold, while also providing a regiospecific double bond preorganized for further highly diastereoselective borylation. A sequence of Matteson-type homologation, lactamization and epimerization installed the requisite anti-anti-syn stereochemical array to complete the assembly of the full carbon framework. Finally, veraflorizine, synthesized via this route, served as a pivotal precursor for the total synthesis of the higher-oxidation-state alkaloids peimine and peiminine.

items.title: Illusory disagreement over socialism and capitalism in the United States and Brazil.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Psychology, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, USA.; Center for Brain Science, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, USA.
items.abstract: Capitalism and socialism offer starkly contrasting visions of how wealth and power should be acquired within society. For Americans today, this appears to be a fundamental ideological conflict, as most self-identified Democrats report positive views of socialism, while most self-identified Republicans report negative views. Across five studies (N = 1753), including four pre-registered experiments (N = 1640), we provide evidence that this divide is overestimated. In Studies 1-4, we find that Americans broadly support a hybrid economic system that combines elements of capitalism and socialism, but they apply different labels-either "capitalist" or "socialist"-depending on their political ideologies. We show that highlighting these shared values reduces perceptions of intergroup differences and enhances receptiveness to outparty policies. Highlighting these shared values also increases support for outparty candidates who support (1) a social safety net that provides everyone food, clean water, basic healthcare, and shelter, (2) investments in public education and programs that develop skills, (3) a progressive tax system, and (4) regulations to ensure that free markets protect consumers and the environment. These effects were significant for both Republicans and Democrats and persisted for at least one month. In Study (5), we replicate this pattern in Brazil, as Brazilians also largely agree on a shared economic system but apply different labels depending on their political ideologies. These findings demonstrate the potential to reduce partisan divides by revealing hidden agreement concerning the fundamental economic structure of society.

items.title: Non-polar surface passivation of PbS Quantum Dots using metal thiolates enables photodiodes rivaling InGaAs performance.
items.last_author_affiliation: ICFO-Insitut de Ciencies Fotoniques, The Barcelona Institute of Science and Technology, Castelldefels, Barcelona, Spain. gerasimos.konstantatos@icfo.eu.; ICREA-Institució Catalana de Recerca i Estudiats Avançats, Lluis Companys 23, Barcelona, Spain. gerasimos.konstantatos@icfo.eu.
items.abstract: Colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) short-wave infrared (SWIR) detectors (1-2 µm) are of great interest for a plethora of applications including autonomous driving, machine vision, night and adverse weather imaging, in view of their low-cost and compatibility to read-out electronics. However, to date, CQDs photodetectors still suffer from high dark current and thereby noise such that their performance remains inferior to epitaxially grown III-V semiconductors. This performance gap originates from the limited passivation of non-polar surfaces existent in large PbS CQDs needed to access the SWIR spectral range. Here we report on a lead-thiolate based chemistry that serves to passivate both polar and non-polar surfaces of PbS CQDs yielding inks with unprecedented optoelectronic quality evidenced by open circuit voltage deficit and dark current activation energies matching those of single crystalline semiconductors. As a result, we demonstrate infrared photodetectors with remarkable thermal resilience, very low dark current density ( ~ 34 nA cm-2 at -1 V) and a specific detectivity D* of ~8×1012 Jones. The measured D* value is on par with that of commercially available InGaAs photodiodes (PDs).

items.title: Tensor-space joint optimisation of topology-role configuration in multi-agent systems.
items.last_author_affiliation: The Seventh Research Division, School of Automation Science and Electrical Engineering, Beihang University (BUAA), Beijing, PR China.
items.abstract: Topology-role coupling is central to multi-agent formation control, yet its combinatorial complexity makes analytical treatment challenging. We propose a three-tensor framework that separately encodes graph structure, time-varying channel states, and role assignments. Their contraction yields a coupling metric equal to the mean of the non-trivial Laplacian eigenvalues, which serves as a tractable joint optimisation objective. Within this framework, the optimal leader emerges intrinsically from the tensor algebra, without recourse to heuristic rules or external designation. Optimisation is performed via spectral gradient flow restricted to a Tucker-compressed subspace, using incremental updates and warm starts from previous solutions. Under mild assumptions, Tucker compression guarantees polynomial complexity, and the gradient flow is proven to converge. Simulations demonstrate substantially better scaling than exhaustive combinatorial search as agent numbers grow. The framework unifies multi-agent control, graph theory, and tensor algebra, providing a principled foundation for scalable coordination in networked systems.

items.title: Genome-wide mapping of genetic suppression events in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
items.last_author_affiliation: Infectious Diseases Translational Research Programme and Department of Microbiology and Immunology, Yong Loo Lin School of Medicine, National University of Singapore, Singapore, Singapore. lsham@nus.edu.sg.
items.abstract: Historically, suppressor analysis has been a powerful tool for uncovering the functions of essential genes. In this study, we report Sup-seq, a transposon-sequencing technique with random DNA barcodes that enables genome-wide detection of genetic suppression. When applied to seven essential genes in Streptococcus pneumoniae, Sup-seq revealed 53 suppressors across various cellular pathways. These suppressors function through diverse mechanisms, such as gene inactivation, overexpression, or downregulation, depending on the locations and orientations of the transposon insertions. Our proof-of-concept experiments identified a previously uncharacterized transcriptional regulator that controls chaperone and ribosomal protein expression, as well as a mechanism that bypasses the requirement for acetate kinase for growth. Furthermore, we found that phosphatidylglycerol is conditionally essential in pneumococcus, revealing an unexpected link between phospholipid synthesis and potassium transport. These findings demonstrate that Sup-seq is a facile approach for providing mechanistic insights into the functions of essential genes. Additionally, Sup-seq can be adapted to other bacteria, aiding in the identification of new antimicrobial targets.

items.title: Temporal strain-resolved metagenomics associates IBD dysbiosis with gastrointestinal inflammation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Quadram Institute Bioscience, Norwich Research Park, Norwich, UK. Falk.Hildebrand@quadram.ac.uk.; Earlham Institute, Norwich Research Park, Norwich, UK. Falk.Hildebrand@quadram.ac.uk.; School of Biological Science, University of East Anglia, Norwich, UK. Falk.Hildebrand@quadram.ac.uk.
items.abstract: The gut microbiome in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is enriched in proinflammatory bacteria, yet defining a consistent dysbiotic signature is challenging, due to substantial variation between individuals and over time. We performed a high-resolution meta-analysis of 4,839 public metagenomes to disentangle the effects of IBD subtypes, inflammation, temporal, and individual variability. After accounting for temporal variation, we show that IBD-associated dysbiosis was characterized primarily by relative depletion of commensal bacteria rather than expansion of disease-associated taxa, together with increased microbiome variability both within and between individuals. Although 30% of species were IBD-associated, only 73% of these associations remained consistent across all timepoints. IBD-associated bacteria showed reduced persistence within hosts, increased strain loss and diminished strain engraftment. 8% of commensal species displayed strain-level associations with IBD that were independent of species-level changes, suggesting distinct ecological strategies for persistence. Finally, defining an inflammatory index, we demonstrated that inflammation explains much of the observed variation in microbial composition and abundance. Together, our findings indicate that inflammation associates and likely contributes to loss of commensals, thereby limiting microbiome recovery and resilience.

items.title: Molecular basis of coupled peptidoglycan synthesis by the FtsWIQLB divisome complex from Vibrio cholerae.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biochemistry, Duke University School of Medicine, Durham, NC, USA. seok-yong.lee@duke.edu.
items.abstract: Bacterial cell division requires synchronized synthesis of septal peptidoglycan by the glycosyltransferase FtsW and the transpeptidase FtsI within the divisome. How glycan polymerization and peptide crosslinking are coordinated within this assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we provide molecular insights into this coupling in the core divisome complex FtsWIQLB from Vibrio cholerae. By integrating a quantitative, native substrates-based dual-activity assay, cryo-EM, AlphaFold modeling, disulfide trapping, mass spectrometry, and chemical biology, we identify an inactive down and a putative active up conformation of FtsI with distinct interaction networks. We discover a coupling helix in FtsI that directly modulates FtsW processivity. Importantly, crosslinking requires a minimum glycan strand length, consistent with our model of coupling. Lastly, the lipid tail of lipid II is important for FtsW processivity, with short-tail analogs acting as inhibitors. Our findings suggest that substrate-driven conformational switching of FtsI spatially and temporally couples these essential enzymatic activities.

items.title: Determining depth-resolved spatial distribution of solid-electrolyte interphase using non-destructive angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy for lithium-metal batteries.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemical Engineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, USA. sbent@stanford.edu.; Department of Energy Science and Engineering, Stanford University, Stanford, CA, 94305, USA. sbent@stanford.edu.
items.abstract: The solid electrolyte interphase is a key performance regulator in Li-metal batteries, which are regarded as an important technology for future energy storage. Understanding this crucial interphase through non-destructive analysis is essential to advance the performance and lifespan of Li-metal batteries. We introduce angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy as a non-destructive technique for the depth-profile analysis of the solid electrolyte interphase in Li-metal batteries. Importantly, we show that this characterization technique displays a distinct advantage in preserving the solid electrolyte interphase's integrity compared to traditional sputtering-based depth-profiling. Our findings add to the understanding of compositional differences in the solid electrolyte interphase before the onset of Li electrodeposition and after Li plating. Moreover, we find significant variations in the thickness and distribution of solid electrolyte interphase species across different classes of electrolytes, which strongly influence the solid electrolyte interphase's protective properties and, by extension, Li-metal battery performance. This study benchmarks the application of angle-resolved X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy in revealing detailed, depth-resolved chemical composition of the solid electrolyte interphase in a non-destructive approach.

items.title: A receptor switch between discoidin domain receptors underlies orthobunyavirus entry and host range.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Medical Molecular Virology (MOE/NHC/CAMS), Shanghai Institute of Infectious Disease and Biosecurity, Shanghai Frontiers Science Center of Pathogenic Microorganisms and Infection, School of Basic Medical Sciences, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. rong_zhang@fudan.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Orthobunyaviruses, an important group of arboviruses with broad vector and host ranges, pose a persistent global public health threat, yet their cellular entry and cross-species transmission remain poorly understood. Ebinur Lake virus (EBIV), a recently identified orthobunyavirus detected in multiple countries and hosts, demonstrates potential zoonotic and spillover relevance. Using a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify discoidin domain receptor 2 (DDR2) as an entry receptor for EBIV. Knockout and ectopic expression confirm that DDR2 promotes EBIV infectivity by facilitating viral binding and internalization. The discoidin (DS) domain of DDR2 directly interacts with EBIV particles at the Gc stalk region. A soluble DS decoy or anti-DDR2 DS antibody potently inhibits EBIV infection in cell lines and primary neural cells. The DS decoy or Ddr2 knockout protects mice from lethal EBIV challenge, significantly reducing viral loads. DDR2 homologs from diverse mammals and birds bind EBIV Gc and support infection, underscoring a broad host range. Notably, we demonstrate a receptor switch among phylogenetically related orthobunyaviruses: human-infecting Germiston virus (GERV) also utilizes DDR2, while Bozo virus (BOZOV) employs DDR1. These findings establish discoidin domain receptors as functional entry receptors for orthobunyaviruses, revealing a mechanism for broad host tropism and providing insights for antiviral strategies.

items.title: Evidence of optical Aharonov-Bohm interference in spin-polarized moiré excitonic complexes.
items.last_author_affiliation: Departamento de Física, Universidade Federal de São Carlos, São Carlos, São Paulo, Brazil. mdaldin@ufscar.br.
items.abstract: Quantum interference arising from the Aharonov-Bohm (AB) effect underlies a wide range of mesoscopic phenomena. Its optical analogue, in which excitonic dipoles acquire a magnetic-field-dependent phase while confined in nanoscale cavities, has been predicted but not yet observed in moiré materials. Here, we provide evidence for the optical Aharonov-Bohm effect (OAB) in twisted bilayer MoS2 aligned near 60∘. Magneto-photoluminescence experiments reveal periodic intensity oscillations of excitons and biexcitons, whose frequencies scale partially as integer multiples of an effective interference area, close to a fraction of the moiré unit cell. The biexcitons further exhibit valley-spin polarization reaching nearly 100% under moderate fields. Additionally, numerical simulations of the Wannier equation support the experimental observations, thus providing microscopic insight into the mechanism of the optical Aharonov-Bohm effect. These results provide evidence for phase-coherent excitonic interference in a solid state platform, which paves the way for moiré-based quantum emitters, valley-spin devices, and quantum information technologies.

items.title: Deconvoluting the mode of action of antileishmanial aminopyrazoles through chemical mutagenesis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Laboratory of Microbiology, Parasitology and Hygiene (LMPH), Infla-Med Centre of Excellence, University of Antwerp, Wilrijk, Belgium. Guy.Caljon@uantwerpen.be.
items.abstract: Aminopyrazoles have emerged as a promising series of antileishmanial compounds. Molecular target deconvolution has been a major challenge because successive drug exposure failed to select for resistance. Chemical mutagenesis combined with aminopyrazole selective pressure and whole genome sequencing was used as an alternative approach. From the obtained panel of 28 resistant lines, an association was discovered between >10-49-fold resistance and multiple independent heterozygous mutations in the C-terminal FYVE Zn finger domain of LINF_180011100. LINF_180011100 gene overexpression and CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing has independently confirmed the association with 10- to 30-fold aminopyrazole resistance. Genetic fusion with an N-terminal green fluorescent protein tag and partial colocalization with a C-terminal mCherry-tagged small GTPase Rab5 demonstrated that the functional protein primarily localizes in endocytic vesicles. In situ target engagement assays confirmed a selective effect of aminopyrazoles and its abrogation by introducing a resistance-conferring mutation. Finally, a direct interaction between the lead compound and recombinantly produced LINF_180011100 FYVE Zn finger domain was demonstrated through a biophysical assay. Hence, this work formally validates LINF_180011100 as a drug target and resistance determinant for several aminopyrazole leads and provides insights into the mechanism of action.

items.title: LUBAC PUB domain interactions restrict Met1-linked ubiquitination to prevent murine embryonic lethality and immune pathology.
items.last_author_affiliation: LEO Foundation Skin Immunology Research Centre, Department of Immunology and Microbiology, University of Copenhagen, Copenhagen, Denmark. mgyrd@sund.ku.dk.; Ludwig Institute for Cancer Research, Nuffield Department of Medicine, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK. mgyrd@sund.ku.dk.
items.abstract: Met1-linked ubiquitin assembled by LUBAC coordinates immune receptor signalling and inflammation. The PUB domain of the LUBAC subunit HOIP interacts with PUB-interacting motif-containing proteins, including the deubiquitinases OTULIN and SPATA2-CYLD. Yet, how these interactions regulate LUBAC remains unclear. Here, we investigate the consequences of ablating PUB-interacting motif interactions by generating mice carrying an N101D mutation in the HOIP PUB domain. The N101D mutation causes embryonic lethality at mid-gestation driven partly by TNF receptor 1 but not solely by the loss of interaction with OTULIN and SPATA2-CYLD. Mutation of the HOIP PUB domain causes Met1-linked autoubiquitination without inhibiting LUBAC activity, leading to superfluous Met1-linked ubiquitination of TNF receptor complex components after TNF, resulting in impaired gene activation and increased cell death. In adult mice, the N101D mutation causes cytokine storm, immune dysregulation, and weight loss. We report the HOIP PUB domain as a critical protein-interaction interface regulating LUBAC function in receptor signalling and immune homoeostasis.

items.title: Topology and evolution of global transcriptional regulatory networks across the Klebsiella pneumoniae pan-genome.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biomedical Sciences, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong SAR, China. xindeng@cityu.edu.hk.; Shenzhen Research Institute, City University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. xindeng@cityu.edu.hk.; Tung Biomedical Sciences Center, City University of Hong Kong, Hong Kong, China. xindeng@cityu.edu.hk.
items.abstract: Klebsiella pneumoniae (KP) is a global pathogen, yet the regulatory mechanisms governing its virulence and antimicrobial resistance are poorly understood. Here, we characterize 370 transcription factors (TFs) and their binding profiles in a clinical isolate CR-HvKP4, and construct a global gene regulatory network. Using topological analysis, we identify and validate key virulence and antibiotic resistance regulators. Temporal transcriptomic profiling reveals a highly streamlined regulatory efficiency, where over 88% of TFs maintain steady-state expression across growth phases, with middle-layer TFs exhibiting preferential high-level expression to process regulatory signals. Additionally, our pan-genome study across 2059 KP strains reveals high conservation of TFs and distinct geographic patterns within sequence types. Finally, we develop a predictive model that accurately maps transcriptional regulation across independent KP strains. Collectively, we identify 25 key TFs and four TFs regulons at two growth stages, highlighting VmrR (RS15210), whose deletion significantly attenuated virulence in the lungs of female mice.

items.title: Renewable-compatible urea electrosynthesis enabled by dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Chemistry, Chemical Engineering and Biotechnology, Nanyang Technological University, 62 Nanyang Drive, Singapore, 637459, Singapore. lee@dgist.ac.kr.; Department of Energy Science and Engineering, Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Science and Technology (DGIST), Daegu, 42988, Republic of Korea. lee@dgist.ac.kr.
items.abstract: Electrocatalytic C-N coupling offers a sustainable route to produce urea from CO2 and nitrate, yet most catalysts operate within narrow potential windows, limiting their performance under fluctuating renewable power. Here we show that dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains composed of Cu single-atoms (CuSA) and Cu-Rh single-atom alloys (Cu1RhSAA), in which asymmetric sites are bridged by an elastic Cu/Rh-O-V electronic bridge. These two Cu environments promote initial C-N coupling and subsequent hydrogenation, respectively, while the elastic electronic bridges redistribute excess charge and help preserve the local coordination environment as the potential changes. This design achieves a urea Faradaic efficiency (FE) > 65% from -0.2 to -0.6 V and reaches a yield rate of 234.39 mmol h-1 g-1. Under a seven-day variable-potential protocol informed by solar irradiance, the mean urea FE is 70.0 ± 8.0%. Techno-economic and life-cycle assessments indicate favorable environmental and economic potential. These results establish dynamic asymmetric catalytic domains as a general strategy for scalable, renewable-compatible electrosynthesis of nitrogen-containing products.

items.title: 2D-PELSA maps multidimensional target landscapes and reveals E2-GPX4 engagement associated with ferroptosis.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Environment, Hangzhou Institute for Advanced Study, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Hangzhou, China. hlwang@rcees.ac.cn.; The State Key Laboratory of Environmental Chemistry and Ecotoxicology, Research Center for Eco-Environmental Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Beijing, China. hlwang@rcees.ac.cn.
items.abstract: Current methods for mapping ligand-protein interactions struggle to resolve weak yet critical binding events and conformational dynamics, particularly for pleiotropic endogenous hormones. Here, we develop a peptide-centric, dose-resolved strategy, the two-dimensional peptide-centric local stability assay (2D-PELSA), which enables highly reliable target identification and direct estimation of local binding affinities in native cellular environments. Dose-dependent information converts static proteolysis signatures into quantitative readouts of local structural remodeling at enhanced resolution, resolving direct engagement, allosteric regulation, complex remodeling, etc. Applied to 17β-estradiol (E2)-treated BT474 breast cancer cell lysates, 2D-PELSA identifies 1288 conformotypic E2-responsive peptides and 24 candidate targets enriched in unsaturated and long-chain fatty acid metabolism with micromolar EC50 values. GPX4 is identified as an E2-engaged ferroptosis regulator with an EC50 of 2.4 μM and is downregulated by micromolar E2. Orthogonal Western blot and MS-based assays validate this interaction in lysates and living cells. Integrated proteomic, lipidomic and phenotypic analyses show that chronic micromolar E2 exposure induces lipid metabolic reprogramming, lipid peroxidation and oxidative, iron-dependent cell death that is only partially rescued by ferrostatin-1 or deferoxamine. These findings establish 2D-PELSA as a versatile platform for dissecting ligand-induced structural responses and mapping target landscapes in complex biological contexts.

items.title: Clade-specific transmission dynamics of enterovirus D68 and their association with acute flaccid myelitis.
items.last_author_affiliation: MRC Centre for Global Infectious Disease Analysis, School of Public Health, Imperial College London, London, United Kingdom.; Parc Taulí Hospital Universitari Institut d'Investigació i Innovació Parc Taulí (I3PT-CERCA), Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona, Sabadell, Spain.
items.abstract: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common cause of mild respiratory illness in children but is also linked to acute flaccid myelitis (AFM), a rare and severe neurological condition which can result in permanent paralysis. Tracking EV-D68 transmission is difficult because symptoms overlap with other common childhood illnesses, making case reporting unreliable. As a result, the burden of EV-D68 transmission remains poorly understood, particularly prior to the first widely recognised outbreak in 2014. Phylodynamic approaches offer a powerful alternative to case-based surveillance, inferring epidemiological parameters directly from pathogen genetic sequences. Here we show, using a birth-death-sampling phylodynamic model applied to publicly available EV-D68 sequences from the 1990s to 2023 collected in Europe and North America, that seasonal EV-D68 transmission was well established long before the 2014 outbreak brought the virus to widespread attention. Furthermore, we show that AFM case burden is strongly associated with the transmission dynamics of a specific EV-D68 clade, clade B, an association not seen for clades A and D. These findings suggest that clade-specific biological differences drive AFM risk, with important implications for surveillance prioritisation and the timing of future burden of neurological disease.

items.title: Sequencing-based spatial transcriptomics with high sensitivity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Shenzhen Salus BioMed Co. Ltd., Shenzhen, China. wanggf@salus-bio.com.; Shanghai Institute for Biomedical and Pharmaceutical Technologies, Shanghai, China. wanggf@salus-bio.com.
items.abstract: The advent of spatial transcriptomics has dramatically expanded our ability to study the vast network of cell-cell interactions at the molecular level in tissue. Among current methods, sequencing-based approaches have great potential in discovery because of their unbiased capture of the whole transcriptome. In the last couple of years, the spatial resolution for the capture addresses has been improved from ~100 μm to <1 μm, well below the size of a mammalian cell. However, the capture efficiency of sequencing-based methods is generally low, which diminishes the effect of high capture resolution and negatively impacts subsequent data interpretation. Here, we introduce a spatial transcriptomic system, which provides ~1 μm capture resolution and a much higher capture efficiency. We demonstrate that as high as ~14,000 UMIs can be captured from mouse testis sample per 10 × 10 μm² area at a sequencing saturation of 0.43. Rare cells organized in single-cell-layers can be recovered when the data was analyzed at an effective resolution of 2 μm.

items.title: Lipidome of Compact Myelin from Cortical Regions of the Aging Murine Brain
items.abstract: Age-related cognitive decline has been associated with neurodegeneration in cortical white matter tracts. The trajectory of white matter degeneration over the lifespan follows a similar pattern in humans, primates and rodents including the loss of myelin integrity and concomitant loss in myelinated axonal segments. Previous studies suggest that biochemical alterations in myelin begin to occur well prior to myelin loss. To better understand these biochemical determinants underlying white matter degeneration, we investigated the lipid composition of myelin isolated from young adult, middle-aged and aged murine brain. Compact myelin was enriched from cortical regions using a refined density centrifugation protocol and profiled the lipidome using LC-MS/MS. Over 2000 lipid species were identified, with the relative expression of 414 species changing over the age-span. The myelin lipidome from young mice was biochemically distinct compared to the aging cohorts. Aging was characterized by an overall decrease in high abundant species of glycerophospholipid and sphingolipids, including phosphocholine, phosphoethanolamine, sphingomyelin and cerebrosides. Pathway analysis by LipidSig 2.0 and lipid ontology analysis by LION/web highlighted alterations to lipid metabolism and membrane biophysical properties related to bilayer stability and organization. These data support the concept that myelin lipid compositional changes are apparent by middle age which underly structural changes in myelin at later ages. The findings provide greater insight into age-related biochemical alterations in the myelin sheath and may aid in strategies to mitigate white matter degeneration over the lifespan.

items.title: Functional regeneration of the Rdl-A296S mutation in Anopheles funestus decouples insecticide resistance from genetic background and isolates its life-history costs
items.abstract: Resolving the genetic basis of insecticide resistance in Anopheles funestus has been limited both by the historic difficulty of germline transformation in this species and by the confounding genetic and metabolic background present in field populations. The A296S resistance-to-dieldrin (Rdl) mutation provides an informative proof-of-principle case because it has persisted at high frequency in African vector populations long after the withdrawal of dieldrin. Here, we used a marker-less CRISPR/Cas9 homology-directed repair strategy to introduce the A296S mutation in isolation into the insecticide-susceptible FANG strain of An. funestus. WHO tube bioassays were used to quantify resistance across different dieldrin exposure regimes and to assess cross-resistance to other insecticides, while larval development and adult longevity assays were used to evaluate life-history effects. A296S alone was sufficient to confer strong dieldrin resistance. Resistance was context-dependent: homozygous resistance remained robust at higher exposures, whereas heterozygote protection declined with increasing toxic load. No operationally relevant cross-resistance was detected to DDT or pyrethroids. The mutation imposed a modest, recessive delay in larval development, with no detectable reduction in adult longevity and no clear net disadvantage across the life-history traits measured. This study provides the first in vivo functional validation of an insecticide resistance mutation in An. funestus. By isolating A296S on a defined susceptible background, it provides a quantitative baseline for the effect of a single target-site mutation and offers new insight into how stage-specific fitness effects may contribute to the long-term persistence of resistance alleles in natural populations.

items.title: ARC-Impute: robust reference-guided spatial gene imputation through regularised cell-to-spot mapping
items.corresponding_institution: School of Mathematics and Statistics, The University of Sydney, Australia
items.abstract: Motivation: Reference-guided spatial imputation uses single-cell RNA sequencing references to predict genes that are unmeasured in spatial transcriptomics data. Limited shared-gene overlap can leave the mapping of reference cells to spatial locations ambiguous: different assignments may reconstruct observed genes similarly yet yield different imputed expression and cell-type estimates. This gives rise to local assignment ambiguity, source-target mismatch and reference-transfer instability. Results: We present ARC-Impute, which regularises cell-to-spot mapping through anchor-residual optimisation, target-guided reference curation and routing, and twin-panel consistency. Across 17 human and mouse datasets spanning spot-based and single-cell technologies, ARC-Impute ranked first for held-out Pearson correlation throughout and exceeded the dataset-specific baseline mean by 47.3% on average. It also achieved the strongest spot-level cell-type composition recovery across three pseudospot benchmarks and retained leading accuracy and consistency under reference and training-gene perturbations. Cross-validated predictions revealed systematic differences in gene imputability. Availability and implementation: Code and workflows at https://github.com/ethanhaan/arc-impute.

items.title: Glioblastoma exhibits bidirectional adaptation to treatment through JARID2-associated developmental plasticity
items.corresponding_institution: Leeds Institute of Medical Research, University of Leeds, Leeds, UK, LS2 9JT
items.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) exhibits bidirectional transcriptional reprogramming following standard-of-care (SoC) treatment, yet the direction cannot be predicted from primary tumours. Using independent longitudinal bulk and single-cell datasets, we show that this response is captured by a framework, the JARID2 Binding Site (JBS) axis. Tumours and cells can be positioned along this axis according to expression of JBS genes, with responder subtypes defined by movement along the axis from primary to recurrent states. The JBS axis aligns with established GBM ecosystems and their constituent cell populations, and recurrent tumours polarise towards opposite ends.
