This framework enhances generalization across sparse clinical profiles by leveraging deep neural representations for patient-specific and cross-patient parameter learning, and potentially enables the identification of personalized dosing schedules tailored to individual tumor trajectories. Preliminary evaluations confirm that it reliably captures treatment-associated PSA dynamics while overcoming the computational bottlenecks of numerical solvers. Ultimately, this work provides a scalable foundation for optimizing adaptive therapy protocols to extend time to disease progression. We present the architectural formulation, forecasting evaluation against mechanistic baselines, and training and optimization procedures of the deep neural networks.

items.title: Distinct roles of microglial and neuronal P2X4 in persistent neuropathic pain
items.abstract: Neuropathic pain is a chronic, debilitating condition characterized by persistent sensory hypersensitivity and frequently associated with anxiety- and depression. Although microglial P2X4 receptors are well-established mediators of early neuropathic pain, their cell-specific contributions to pain maintenance and associated affective disturbances remains poorly understood. We investigated these contributions in male and female mice 30 and 60 days after spared nerve injury (SNI) using conditional P2X4 deletion in microglia (Cx3cr1CreERT2) or neurons (Synapsin-1-Cre), behavioral assessments, and in vivo recordings of spinal dorsal horn wide dynamic range neurons. Microglial P2X4 deletion before SNI completely prevented mechanical allodynia whereas deletion initiated 40 days after injury fully reversed established allodynia in both sexes. Notably, P2X4 immunoreactivity was undetectable in spinal microglia at the late time points examined, suggesting that the sustained contribution of microglial P2X4 may involve mechanisms outside the spinal microglial compartment. Neuronal P2X4 deletion partially attenuated mechanical hypersensitivity and reduced dorsal horn neurons hyperexcitability at day 60 after SNI, supporting a modulatory role in persistent spinal sensitization. Global P2X4 deletion prevented anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors that emerged by day 30 in males and day 60 in females. Whether this protection reflects a direct contribution of P2X4 to affective disturbances or an indirect consequence of reduced pain remains unresolved. Together, these findings identify distinct microglial and neuronal P2X4 contributions to established neuropathic pain and reveal sex-dependent differences in the onset of associated affective disturbances.

items.title: TSPAN10 Loss-of-Function in hESC-Derived RPE Reveals Critical Roles in Pigmentation, Polarity, and Antioxidant Defence
items.abstract: Expression quantitative trait loci studies have highlighted TSPAN10 as a gene that confers an increased risk of developing age-related macular degeneration (AMD). The mechanism for this and the role of TSPAN10 in retinal cells such as the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) and its contribution to AMD pathology are unknown. We report the generation of human embryonic stem cell derived RPE with TSPAN10 knockout using CRISPR/Cas9 genome editing. This provided an in vitro model to investigate the functions of TSPAN10. TSPAN10 knockout cells were differentiated into mature RPE. Significant differences were observed in cell pigmentation, polarisation and cell body height, and the response to oxidative stress in comparison to wild type. These results demonstrate for the first time a role for TSPAN10 in the RPE, aligning with published data to support the importance of TSPAN10 for pigmentation, and adding to our understanding of the heterogeneous disease AMD.

items.title: 5-HT2A receptor deletion is associated with reduced hippocampal parvalbumin levels and anxiety-like behavior in BALB/c mice
items.abstract: The serotonin 2A receptor (5-HT2AR) is a target of drugs used to treat anxiety and mood disorders, yet whether endogenous 5-HT2AR signaling constrains or promotes anxiety, and how the 5-HT2AR affects cell populations linked to anxiety, is not fully resolved. Acute 5-HT2AR agonism is anxiolytic and acts through the activation of ventral hippocampal parvalbumin-expressing interneurons. Here we report that constitutive deletion of the 5-HT2AR in male and female BALB/c mice is associated with robust anxiety-like and repetitive behavior across multiple paradigms. Unbiased proteomic analysis of male knockout hippocampal tissue revealed substantially reduced levels of parvalbumin (PV), a proxy of their activity. Consistent with the intense metabolic demands of fast spiking interneurons, proteins supporting energy metabolism were also downregulated, including those related to oxidative phosphorylation and the electron transport chain, glycolysis and the tricarboxylic acid cycle, together with the cytoplasmic ribosome. In terms of how reduced 5-HT2AR signaling could lead to reduced PV expression, we examined key perineuronal net (PNN) components. The PNN constituents aggrecan and HAPLN1 were not significantly changed, whereas the link protein, HAPLN4 was substantially reduced. In a separate cohort, 7 days following a single dose of the selective 5-HT2AR agonist, 25CN-NBOH, many of the same energy metabolism proteins were shifted in the opposite direction. Together these findings indicate that constitutive loss of 5-HT2AR signaling is associated with coordinated reductions in parvalbumin and in the biosynthetic and bioenergetic machinery that supports fast-spiking activity, without a generalized loss of perineuronal net structural components.

items.title: How reliable is the link between effort and nucleus accumbens connectivity at rest? A psychometric evaluation of repeated assessments
items.corresponding_institution: Section of Medical Psychology, Department of Psychiatry and Psychotherapy, Faculty of Medicine, University of Bonn, Bonn, Germany
items.abstract: Individuals differ in their willingness to work for rewards. Although effort-based behavior shows trait-like stability and motivational traits associate with functional connectivity (FC), it remains unclear how robustly individual differences in effort are reflected in intrinsic FC of reward circuits. Here, we investigated whether effort-based behavior and questionnaire scores are reflected in nucleus accumbens (NAcc) FC. To this end, we evaluated this association in 84 healthy adults (43 women, 41 men), who completed five sessions of an effort allocation task and two task-free fMRI scans, each collected on different days to capture trait-like behavior and brain function. First, behavioral measures showed high test-retest reliability across sessions (ICCs: 0.62-0.83). Second, NAcc FC showed the highest reliability in subcortical regions (ICCs = 0.59-0.69), while cortical connections were heterogeneous and, overall, less reliable. Higher effort exertion was associated with stronger NAcc<>IFG FC (tmax(76) = 4.65, pFWE = .041, k = 141), while greater sensitivity to task difficulty was associated with stronger NAcc<>subcallosal gyrus FC (tmax(76) = -5.15, pFWE = .028, k = 155). Intriguingly, the association of effort exertion with NAcc<>IFG FC decreased over behavioral sessions, whereas the association of sensitivity to cost (difficulty) with NAcc<>subcallosal FC was stable over behavioral sessions. Our findings show that identifying robust brain-behavior associations likely requires comparable multi-session approaches, at least in moderately sized samples. Beyond reliability, such approaches may also help reveal additional insights about the temporal profile of brain-behavior associations, which may differ markedly for new versus routine task performance.

items.title: Lightness illusions and saliency maps for reflectance estimation are similar across a wide range of deep neural network architectures
items.abstract: People perform many visual tasks that depend on having representations that remain correlated with surface reflectance despite large variations in illumination and context. This ability is known as `lightness constancy'. Developing image-computable models of lightness constancy has been challenging, but we recently showed that deep neural networks trained for reflectance estimation achieve good performance on some lightness tasks, and furthermore are susceptible to many of the same lightness illusions as human observers. Here we extend this work by testing whether these findings are specific to the network architecture we used in our previous work, or whether they generalize broadly across architectures and training procedures. We evaluated a range of architectures (ResUNet, VGGUNet, MobileUNet, and Dense Prediction Transformer) that we trained to estimate reflectance from rendered images of three-dimensional scenes. We compared networks where the initial, stimulus-encoding phase used pre-trained weights learned for other tasks, and networks where all weights were optimized for reflectance estimation. We found that all architectures and training procedures tested produced similar reflectance estimation performance on held-out images, and were susceptible to several classic lightness illusions. Furthermore, saliency analyses showed that all networks had broadly similar spatial sensitivity across input images. Together, these results suggest that lightness constancy and susceptibility to lightness illusions do not depend strongly on details of network architecture and training, but instead often emerge robustly in networks that have been optimized to infer surface reflectance from luminance.

items.title: Network-related variations of cerebrovascular status are correlated with cognitive control performance
items.abstract: Cerebrovascular health has emerged as a crucial factor in influencing cognitive decline in aging, including cognitive control and fluid intelligence. Previous studies have largely relied on peripheral assessments of vascular health due to the paucity of global and regional estimates of cerebrovascular status. This study uses the pulse relaxation function (PReFx), a measure of pulse-wave shape based on diffuse optical tomography (pulse-DOT), to provide regional estimates of arterial elasticity in the cortical mantle. For the first time, we integrate a network-based approach based on previous fMRI studies and pulse-DOT regional mapping of cerebrovascular status, to test whether the support provided by the cerebrovascular system to different brain networks may differentially impact cognitive control performance. To comprehensively assess how various mechanisms of cognitive control are influenced by the cerebrovascular health of different networks, we used a task-switching paradigm that simultaneously measures proactive and reactive control processes. After removing the global signal, we found that larger positive PReFx residual values in the Dorsal Attention and Visual Networks are linked to lower cognitive control costs. Conversely, larger positive residual values in the Default Mode and Fronto-Parietal Networks are associated with higher cognitive control costs. These results indicate that the relative balance of arterial elasticity across different brain networks impacts cognitive control, highlighting the importance of studying network-based cerebrovascular status for understanding cognitive performance.

items.title: Social environment induces reversible remodeling of the adult primate brain
items.abstract: Patterns of social contact can change abruptly, but whether their effects on brain architecture persist or recede when original conditions return remains unclear. Here we followed 13 adult male macaques through three successive phases of single housing, protected-contact paired housing, and restored single housing, acquiring structural and functional MRI and measuring hair cortisol at approximately three-month intervals, with two assessments per phase. Paired housing was associated with grey-matter expansion across temporal association cortex and several subcortical and brainstem structures. Concurrently, default-mode- and limbic-associated regions shifted within a functional-connectivity manifold, while hair cortisol increased. When single housing was restored, grey-matter and cortisol elevations receded, and regional functional changes reversed direction. These trajectories identify a reversible component of adult primate brain architecture that tracks current social conditions.

items.title: Functional cell type diversity in the Drosophila lamina is established by a single transcription factor dFezf, controlling a large repertoire of ion channels and receptors
items.abstract: Neuronal cell types in the brain can show remarkable diversity in their functional properties. In the visual system, neurons at different levels of hierarchy show diverse kinetics, leading to the encoding of different features of the visual scene. How this behaviorally relevant diversification is achieved is not understood. Here, we address this question in a simple system, studying two visual cell types in Drosophila that diversify their responses despite receiving the same photoreceptor input to encode two distinct basic visual features, contrast and luminance. We first show that this cell type diversity is mostly established by cell-intrinsic mechanism. While cell-type specific transcriptome analysis delivers promising receptor and channel candidates, genetic manipulation of these differentially regulated genes fails to identify individual channels or receptors that are necessary or sufficient for the functional differences between luminance-sensitive L3 neurons and contrast-sensitive L2 neurons. However, loss of the L3-specific transcription factor dFezf makes L3 neurons transient and contrast-sensitive. Interestingly, dFezf controls the cell-type-specific expression of several receptors and ion channels that we initially found to be differentially expressed between L2 and L3. Together, this argues for a degenerate system in which multiple genes jointly shape cell type-specific functional properties. Our finding that a single transcription factor regulates the expression of such a set of genes that can be relevant for function suggest that similar regulation might also be in place in other degenerate systems, which exist widely across cell types, brain regions, and species.

items.title: Tissue-specific mucociliary regulatory programs in the healthy human endocervix and ectocervix
items.abstract: The cervix is a dynamic mucosal barrier in the female reproductive tract that balances inflammatory and anti inflammatory functions to regulate physiologically critical functions, including pregnancy, sperm transport, fertility, and protection of the upper reproductive tract from infection. Despite its central role in reproduction, the cellular and transcriptional organization of the healthy human cervix remains incompletely characterized, including how clinical sampling methods influence the epithelial populations recovered and how cervical mucociliary programs compare with those of pulmonary epithelium. We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNAseq) on paired Tischler punch biopsy and endocervical curettage (ECC) samples from four healthy, exogenous hormone-naive donors to generate a dedicated transcriptomic map of the healthy human cervix followed by an integrative computational analysis framework combining differential expression, functional enrichment, cell to cell communication, cross-tissue mapping, and regulon activity inference. This approach identified ten cell types spanning epithelial, stromal, vascular, and immune cell populations and found that sampling method strongly influenced cellular composition and transcriptional state as Tischler punch biopsy preferentially recovered basal and suprabasal epithelial populations, whereas ECC enriched for secretory and ciliated epithelial cell types. Cross-tissue comparison with publicly available healthy lung epithelial transcriptomics dataset revealed conserved mucociliary cell types alongside tissue-divergent transcriptional programs, including distinct regulation of ion transport and mucin associated genes. Together, these findings demonstrate the importance of sampling modality in resolving cervical epithelial heterogeneity, and reveal tissue-specialized mucociliary regulatory programs underlying cervical mucus biology and fertility regulation.

items.title: SOUR Disentangles Heritable and Microenvironmental Contributions to Intratumoral Heterogeneity in Spatial Lineage Tracing Data
items.abstract: Intratumoral heterogeneity is hypothesized to be a major contributor to treatment resistance, yet the processes that generate it remain only partially understood. New technologies enable measurement of gene expression in individual tumor cells while also determining where the cells are located within a tumor and how they are related through cell division. A central question for such data is how much gene expression differences reflect characteristics passed from parent cells to their descendants, rather than influences from their local surroundings. Distinguishing these influences is challenging because closely related cells often reside near one another. Existing methods examine the relationship between gene expression and each of these factors separately, and can therefore incorrectly attribute spatial effects to ancestry or inherited effects to spatial location. Here, we present SOUR, a statistical method that uses both cell ancestry and spatial location to estimate their respective contributions to differences in gene expression. Using simulated data and two spatial lineage tracing datasets, we demonstrate that SOUR can estimate the separate contributions of cell ancestry and spatial location to variation in gene expression, while substantially reducing the confounding observed with existing approaches.

items.title: Curated annotations locate biological concepts in protein language models from layers to neurons
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Biomedical Engineering, University of Delaware
items.abstract: Interpretability methods describe what a network has learned, yet their claims are rarely tested against model-independent ground truth. We argue that proteins are an ideal modality for interpretability since curators annotate functional sites residue by residue. Across three ESMC protein language models (300M-6B parameters), we show that conclusions depend on where models are read, how concepts are decoded, which units are examined, and how they are scored. Concepts become linearly readable along depth long before erasure impairs masked-token prediction, and 20-fold scaling shifts concept depth more than peak score. Most of a nonlinear probe's lead over a linear one reflects fitting and readout shape rather than nonlinear encoding. Over whole proteins, saturated metrics render feed-forward neurons indistinguishable from random rotations. At annotated residues, dual-signed neuron poles identify 2.5-5.4 times as many concepts as rotations without training, though sparse autoencoders identify more. Without held-out validation, however, shuffled annotations label nearly every latent, and causal reliance emerges in neuron groups rather than single poles. Reading selected intra-block states exposes binding and active sites that stream probes read poorly and lifts a simple probe 5% above the best published MCC on a leakage-controlled interaction benchmark. We recommend reading a model directly against annotation, scoring units where they fire with a measure that is not saturated, and training a dictionary only where it adds coverage.

items.title: Systematic inference of biological relatedness across the global ancient DNA record
items.corresponding_institution: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology
items.abstract: The rapidly expanding scale of ancient DNA data creates an increasing need for high-performance software methods. One area for such improvement is the inference of pairwise biological relatedness, a prominent aspect of many ancient DNA studies. We present fastpmr, a fast and memory-efficient method for biological relatedness inference based on the computation of pairwise mismatch rates. We demonstrate that fastpmr can achieve over 1000x speed-up over READv2, a widely used relatedness-inference method. We leverage this performance to investigate relatedness at the scale of the global ancient DNA record. Analyzing biological relatedness across all pairs in the Allen Ancient DNA Resource (n = 19,118 ancient and 23,089 total samples) recapitulates human evolutionary history and identifies previously unknown genetic duplicates and likely sample mix-ups, demonstrating fastpmr's utility for ancient DNA analysis and quality control at scale.

items.title: Trial history and model-derived reward prediction errors in mousevisual decisions
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Psychology, University of Freiburg, Freiburg, Germany
items.abstract: A reward prediction error (RPE) estimated from an animal's behavior can predict its next choice. Part of this predictive value may come from information about earlier trials that a choice model could also use directly. We asked whether a model-derived RPE improves choice prediction beyond the observable history of stimuli, choices, and rewards. We analyzed 275,292 trials from 107 mice performing the International Brain Laboratory visual decision task and evaluated the main choice models on sessions that were not used for fitting. Recent choices strongly improved prediction. An RPE based on a stimulus-dependent reward expectation added a small gain beyond the preceding choice and reward, and this gain fell to near zero once the model included the preceding stimulus. When the model also summarized choices and rewards over several earlier trials, an RPE trace with the same retention parameter as the history traces did not reliably improve prediction. In simulated agents with known decision rules, a simplified version of this comparison detected an RPE-based learning rule in which choices depended on accumulated prediction errors, and did not improve prediction for an agent that used trial history directly. In mice, the state-dependent RPE and its trace added little predictive information beyond observable trial history, which limits what choice prediction alone can reveal about prediction-error learning.

items.title: PolyMorph3D: A flexible MATLAB-based tool for quantifying microglia morphology and multi-colocalization in three dimensions
items.corresponding_institution: University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine
items.abstract: As the principle immune cell of the central nervous system (CNS), microglia have been extensively studied throughout development and in a wide range of disease states. Of special focus have been their morphological features such as branching complexity, physical cell-cell interactions with surroundings, and gene expression readouts relating to phagocytosis and cytokine signaling. Each of these domains offers a window onto microglia function, and high-resolution confocal microscopy has long been a workhorse technique to visualize all three. A comprehensive view of microglia function requires both high-fidelity quantification with 3D resolution and colocalization of microglia with functional proteins such as those related to phagocytosis and with nearby structures such as synapses. Accordingly, a number of analytical tools have been developed to measure these features. However, existing open-source options lack either colocalization or 3D capability, while commercial solutions can be costly. Here, we sought to develop an open-source solution that addresses each of these limitations. PolyMorph3D is a MATLAB-based program capable of yielding individual cell-level data of microglia morphology and overlap with up to 4 other sources, all in 3D. The pipeline can be used effectively in mouse tissue and in human postmortem brain, thereby offering a flexible, low cost, and high-fidelity solution for the analysis of microglial morphology and function.

items.title: When spike sorting matters: single-neuron identity in the quantification of neural circuits
items.abstract: Multiunit threshold crossings support high-performance brain-computer interfaces and preserve the low-dimensional trajectories that summarize population dynamics, raising the question of when spike sorting is still necessary. Using previously published recordings from four rhesus monkeys, we analyzed areas 3b and 1 of primary somatosensory cortex and ventral premotor cortex during a bimodal detection task, and ventral premotor cortex during an interval comparison task. From the same spikes, we built three representations: putative single units obtained with nonlinear sorting (UMAP and HDBSCAN), intermingled units obtained with linear sorting, and unsorted multiunit activity. Nonlinear sorting resolved up to three times more units than multiunit activity. In area 1, mixing discarded the periodicity information carried by phase-locked neurons, lengthened intrinsic timescales by about 40%, increased trial-to-trial variability, and raised neurometric detection thresholds by 33%. In premotor cortex, mixing reduced the task-related information recovered from the population and hid significant dimensions of its dynamics. After geometric alignment, the overall shape of population trajectories was nearly identical across representations, but distances between population states were distorted, and the approximately linear representation of interval duration saturated for longer intervals. Multiunit activity is therefore sufficient for analyses that rely on the dominant, shared structure of population activity, such as decoding, whereas analyses of single-neuron coding, variability, timescales, dimensionality, and parametric representations often require spike sorting.

items.title: BrainRoute integrates machine learning prediction with community-driven verification of blood-brain barrier permeability
items.corresponding_institution: Institute for Genomic Medicine Research, West Hartford, CT, USA
items.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) is a highly selective barrier that restricts the entry of many therapeutic agents into the brain. The lack of efficient methods for BBB permeability research and data management remains a significant challenge for central nervous system drug-development pipelines. Although BBB permeability data are available from multiple open sources, few platforms integrate these datasets with molecular exploration, predictive tools, and a structured process for community-supported data verification. Here, we present BrainRoute, an open platform for BBB molecular data collection, exploration, prediction, and community-supported verification. BrainRoute provides searchable and filterable molecular records, physicochemical and structural information, source-linked data, single-molecule and batch prediction, and a structured workflow through which users can submit additional evidence for review. The prediction tool model-development cohort contained 7,888 unique molecules, including 5,424 BBB+ and 2,464 BBB- molecules. Six machine-learning classifiers were evaluated using PaDEL descriptors, Morgan fingerprints, frozen ChemBERTa embeddings, and combined feature representations. The three selected models were integrated into the platform as a probability-averaged ensemble. The primary five-fold scaffold-grouped analysis achieved a best mean balanced accuracy of 0.783 {+/-} 0.026. On an independent external set containing 410 non-overlapping molecules, the deployed ensemble achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.659 (95% CI 0.600 - 0.712) and an AUPRC of 0.670 (95% CI 0.583 - 0.752). BrainRoute serves as a platform for exploring BBB-related molecular data and computational predictions while supporting the continued growth and verification of the underlying dataset. BrainRoute is freely accessible online (https://github.com/omicscodeathon/brainroutedb).

items.title: Harmonizing resting-state functional MRI data to increase sample size and to classify tinnitus brain connectivity
items.abstract: Tinnitus, or ringing in the ears, is a hearing disorder that affects approximately 15% of human adults globally. The neuroscientific understanding of this subjective disorder is limited at present, partly due to a lack of sufficient neuroimaging data to compensate for the heterogeneity in the disorder; neural data acquisition is often impeded by low patient counts and doubled costs against scanning ample controls. However, with the increase in data sharing practices, data scarcity can be overcome with harmonization methods if scans from independent sites and studies are pooled successfully. To achieve data harmonization for limited data from a tinnitus neuroimaging study, we merged a modest fMRI dataset acquired in our lab (n=35) with age- and gender-matched samples from another large dataset, the Lifespan Human Connectome Project Aging (n=377). We measured functional connectivity (FC) between brain regions based on resting-state fMRI session scans, and used deep learning architecture to systematically combine individual FCs across the datasets. We assembled and trained neural network modules to purge dataset-identifying information from FC maps, and retained patterns that can characterize tinnitus-related FC. Hallmark artifactual information of the datasets was significantly reduced while reconstructing resting state FC data. Relevant relationships in brain connectivity that discern the condition of tinnitus from controls were well-preserved in the reconstructed resting state FC data. In agreement with existing literature on brain networks of tinnitus, connectivity related to default mode, ventral attention and frontoparietal control networks were identified to be crucial for distinguishing the condition, as masking these networks connections severely impacted downstream classification prediction on reconstructed FC. The data harmonization model was successful in merging FC matrices from independently acquired fMRI datasets, without losing out on meaningful functional connectivity patterns of interest for the neuropsychological disorder of tinnitus. Our findings demonstrate the potential of data harmonization by integrating independently acquired datasets on healthy controls to overcome neuroimaging data scarcity while preserving disorder-relevant neural signatures, advancing research on understudied neurological disorders.

items.title: Early Life Shift in Fear Extinction is Driven by Prefrontal-Amygdala Engagement
items.abstract: The medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) displays a delayed maturation long hypothesized to guide developmental changes in threat processing. Nevertheless, the mechanism by which ontogenetic changes in mPFC function guide the developmental emergence of behavior is unclear. Early life marks a shift between a permanent extinction phenotype typical of juveniles, toward the standard, more transient extinction seen in adult rodents. This shift coincides with developmental changes in mPFC-amygdala connectivity, a pathway necessary for extinction processing in adults. Here we used optogenetics and slice electrophysiology to show that, in contrast to adult animals, juvenile mice displaying permanent extinction fail to engage the mPFC-amygdala pathway at the synaptic, cell activity or behavioral levels. Consistent with a requirement of this pathway for the developmental transition in extinction types, optic potentiation of the mPFC-amygdala pathway accelerates the onset of adult extinction. Our findings show that the developmental onboarding of the mPFC-amygdala pathway drives a shift in extinction processing toward increased fear reemergence that persists throughout adulthood.

items.title: Immunometabolic IRG1-NLRC5 Axis Controls Inflammatory Cell Death
items.abstract: Innate immunity is the first defense against pathogens, sterile injury, and homeostatic perturbations. One key mechanism used by the innate immune system for host defense is inflammatory cell death, PANoptosis, which eliminates infected or damaged cells and releases cytokines and other danger signals that can further propagate the immune response. Given these inflammatory functions, PANoptosis must be tightly regulated to prevent excess inflammation and pathology. Cellular metabolism is a key regulator of innate immunity, yet how metabolic reprogramming regulates innate immune signaling to control cell death, inflammation, and disease remains poorly understood. Here, we identify the immune-responsive gene 1 (IRG1)-itaconate axis as a critical regulator of PANoptosis. Innate immune triggers robustly induced IRG1 expression, leading to itaconate accumulation and driving IRG1-dependent inflammatory cell death. Mechanistically, glutaminolysis fueled IRG1-dependent itaconate synthesis, and inhibition of glutamine metabolism reduced itaconate accumulation and blocked PANoptosis. Furthermore, NAD depletion, a known inducer of NLRC5-mediated PANoptosis that has been connected to hemolytic, infectious, and inflammatory conditions, acted upstream inducing IRG1 expression and promoting NLRC5-PANoptosome assembly. Together, these findings highlight IRG1 as a metabolic node linking innate immunity to PANoptosis, identifying IRG1 as a potential therapeutic target in hemolytic and inflammatory diseases.

items.title: Antibody-Fcγ receptor-driven NOX2 activation during phagocytosis of tumor cells is suppressed by CD47, preventing CD8 T cell engagement and immunotherapeutic responses.
items.abstract: Antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP) contributes to the elimination of antibody-opsonized tumor cells and engagement of adaptive immunity. This process is inhibited by tumor-cell overexpression of CD47. Here, genome-wide CRISPR screens in macrophages identified the NADPH oxidase (NOX2 complex) and the CD47 receptor, SIRP, as regulators of phagosome acidification. Target-cell CD47 suppressed NOX2 generation of reactive oxygen species at antibody densities that support ADCP, revealing distinct CD47-dependent thresholds for ADCP and oxidant generation. CD47 removal from the target cell delayed phagosome acidification in wild-type macrophages, but not in NOX2-deficient macrophages. Consistent with a role for this pathway in antitumor immunity, tumor-opsonizing anti-Tyrp1 therapy allowed clearance of CD47-deficient B16F10 melanoma tumors in approximately 36% of wild-type mice but failed in NOX2-deficient mice. Tumor clearance required CD8 T cells and IFN{gamma}, but perforin was dispensable. CD4 T cell depletion markedly improved tumor clearance. These findings suggest a noncanonical role for CD8 T cells in supporting ADCP-mediated tumor control. Combining anti-Tyrp1 with a mouse-serum-albumin-IL-2 fusion (MSA-IL-2) or PD-1 blockade enabled superior clearance of CD47-deficient tumors in NOX2-deficient mice, but not wild-type mice. Rechallenge experiments distinguished primary tumor clearance from durable immunity, whereby NOX2-deficient mice treated with anti-Tyrp1 and PD-1 blockade lacked rechallenge protection despite high initial cure rates. Conversely, the addition of MSA-IL-2 supported durable protection in both wild-type and NOX2-deficient mice. These results indicate that tumor CD47 functions beyond a "don't-eat-me" signal by controlling NOX2 activity to positively and negatively regulate CD 8 T cell function. Significance CD47-SIRP suppresses NOX2 activation, regulating a critical feedback loop between ADCP and CD8 T cell activation during tumor-opsonizing antibody therapy, suggesting new strategies for cancer immunotherapy targeting tumor surface antigens.

items.title: MSGFLEX: An optimized end-to-end pipeline for proteomics and metaproteomics analysis built on MS-GF+ with a dedicated rescoring model XPECTRA
items.abstract: Mass spectrometry-based proteomics workflows often face competing demands between identification sensitivity, false discovery rate (FDR) control, and computational scalability, particularly for metaproteomic datasets that require searching large and complex sequence databases. Here, we present MSGFLEX, an integrated end-to-end workflow that combines database searching, machine-learning based rescoring, and peptide-to-protein quantitative inference. MSGFLEX integrates three components: SPARX handles raw file conversion, and MS-GF+ database searching; XPECTRA is a cross-validated XGBoost ensemble that rescores peptide-spectrum matches by combining ensemble predictions with MS-GF+ search evidence through noisy-OR fusion model. QUANTIX provides protein quantification through multiple protein rollup strategies. Across four benchmarking datasets, XPECTRA consistently increased peptide and protein identifications relative to Percolator, MS2Rescore, and MSBooster. On a human gut metaproteome dataset, XPECTRA achieved the largest effect size among all methods evaluated (Cohen's d = 0.95; p < 0.0005). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP)-based analysis indicated that XPECTRA learned consistent relationships from spectral and physicochemical features. Database partitioning does not introduce detectable bias in peptide identification or FDR estimation, while QUANTIX's DWrollup provides the most accurate recovery of known protein abundance changes in a ground-truth spike-in benchmark. Together, these results establish MSGFLEX as a scalable and interpretable framework for mass-spectrometry based proteomics and metaproteomics.

items.title: A site-resolved post-translational modification framework for drug-response analysis
items.abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate protein activity and treatment-associated signalling, providing functional information that can connect drug-response estimates with candidate pharmacodynamic measurements. Assessing this information requires a framework that determines its contribution beyond fixed molecular features while retaining the identity of the modified sites underlying model predictions. We developed the PTM Biological Dynamics Layer (PTM-BDL), which integrates typed PTM states with protein sequence, structure-derived and drug chemical features to predict log-transformed half-maximal inhibitory concentration and resistance while providing site-level interpretation through integrated gradients. Retrospective evaluation used source-derived and propagated PTM profiles across biologically distinct BCR-ABL, HDAC/EP300 and EGFR/ERBB2 settings, yielding internal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) between 0.785 and 0.946. Retraining demonstrated a consistent incremental contribution from PTM inputs in K562/CML, with a mean AUROC increase of 0.0268 and positive gains in all five folds, alongside more modest incremental gains in HeLa/HDAC and EGFR/ERBB2. Within K562/CML, CRKL Y207 and STAT5A Y694 retained the leading attribution ranks for their proteins across three seeds, while greater PTM attribution in dasatinib than in cytotoxic drug contexts identified a focused setting for pharmacodynamic investigation. These findings support context-dependent use of PTM information and connect predictive assessment with prioritisation of individual sites, providing a basis for targeted pharmacodynamic measurements and independent experimental validation.

items.title: The creatine transporter SLC6A8 is an immune pressure-exposed metabolic vulnerability in acute myeloid leukemia
items.corresponding_institution: Bloomberg-Kimmel Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy and Department of Oncology, Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine, Baltimore, MD, USA
items.abstract: Chemotherapy imposes metabolic pressure that generates persisting tumor cell states, but whether these adaptations also shape immune evasion is poorly understood. Here, we identify creatine accumulation as a conserved feature of chemotherapy-persisting acute myeloid leukemia (AML) across mouse and human models. Stable-isotope tracing and genetic perturbation show that this is driven predominantly by SLC6A8-mediated creatine uptake rather than de novo synthesis. SLC6A8 was dispensable for AML proliferation and chemotherapy resistance but strongly promoted leukemia persistence under T cell pressure. This effect was independent of phosphocreatine generation and canonical energetic buffering. Instead, SLC6A8 deficiency increased cytokine-driven STAT1 signaling and chromatin remodeling, inducing the expression of antigen-presentation and co-stimulatory molecules, such as MHC-II, CD40, and CD80. Thus, creatine uptake via SLC6A8 is a non-canonical metabolic adaptation that restrains immune-driven remodeling and enables AML immune evasion. These findings link a therapy-induced metabolic adaptation to cytokine responsiveness and reveal SLC6A8 as a targetable vulnerability.

items.title: Velocity-dependent friction in a simple two-oscillator system. II. Regions of stability
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurology, University of Wisconsin School of Medicine and Public Health
items.abstract: In Part I, a gamma friction that follows theta velocity produced theta gamma phase amplitude coupling (PAC) whose strength is a closed-form function of one dimensionless number, kappa;. Here we ask when this coupling destabilizes the gamma oscillator. The friction on gamma is negative during part of every theta cycle, yet gamma stays bounded: as long as it keeps oscillating, the energy gained while theta rises is returned while theta falls, and Liouville' sformula fixes the growth over a theta cycle at the baseline decay, whatever the coupling. Instability arises only in rare large theta cycles in which the friction exceeds critical damping, so that gamma stops oscillating and the gain is no longer returned. The typical trajectory becomes unstable when such cycles, about one in a hundred, outweigh the decay in all the others. This gives a boundary g* {sigma}x = 10, where {sigma}x is the typical theta amplitude set by the fluctuation dissipation theorem; the prediction agrees with a direct Lyapunov scan to within 6% for damping ratios from 0.0005 to 0.0055. The distance to the boundary is set by the same number kappa that sets the PAC strength, so that stronger PAC means closer proximity to instability. The mean-square boundary lies far lower but is set by events of negligible probability. Stimulating theta at or below its own frequency raises gamma energy and PAC and can drive giant gamma bursts or divergence, but no self-sustained activity, suggesting that a transition to seizure requires memory.

items.title: Velocity-dependent friction in a simple two-oscillator system. I. Phase amplitude coupling
items.abstract: Cortical gamma oscillations often arrive in bursts locked to the phase of slower theta waves, a pattern called theta gamma phase amplitude coupling (PAC). PAC is linked to memory and altered in epilepsy, but most models tie it to particular cells or circuits. We start from a generalized Langevin equation, an equation of motion for a few collective variables in which friction and random forces stand for the unobserved neural activity, and let its stiffness and friction depend on the state. Expanding them to first order in the theta and gamma variables yields ten possible interaction terms; only the two friction type terms change gamma energy and produce PAC, and depending on the term and its sign the gamma bursts sit at the peak, trough, rising or falling phase of theta. We study a gamma friction that follows theta velocity as a simplified example. Because the time integral of theta velocity is theta coordinate, the gamma amplitude rises and falls with theta coordinate as exp(gvvx{theta}/2). The fluctuation dissipation theorem turns noise and damping into a theta effective temperature, and the PAC strength becomes a closed form function of one dimensionless number, kappa , that combines the coupling with this temperature. Without fitted parameters, this prediction accounts for 51,095 simulated records (R2 = 0.993) and for the median PAC of 5,160 combinations of coupling and damping (R2 = 0.989). The coupling also drives gamma out of equilibrium: its kinetic temperature grows far above the one inferred from its response. All coefficients enter linearly so that they can, in principle, be estimated from recordings by linear regression. A companion paper shows that the same number sets the distance to a stability boundary.

items.title: Tetrodotoxin-resistant NaV1.8 contributes to action potential conduction in a population of mouse and human vagal nerve fibers
items.abstract: Axonal action potential (AP) conduction is dependent on voltage-gated sodium channels (NaV1s). AP conduction in the vagus nerve (which contains afferent and efferent fibers) is essential to its reflex regulation of most visceral organs. The nine isoforms of NaV1s show diverse expression patterns in vagal neurons. In rodent vagus nerves, multiple NaV1 isoforms contribute to AP conduction, with NaV1.7 playing an essential role in ~70% of fibers. Here, we investigated the contribution of tetrodotoxin-resistant (TTX-R) NaV1.8 towards vagal AP conduction ex vivo. We tested two structurally different NaV1.8-selective inhibitors, A803467 and PF01247324 and their effects on electrically evoked C-fiber compound action potentials (CAPs) along mouse and human vagus nerves. Tetrodotoxin completely abolished mouse and human vagal CAPs. Nevertheless, both A803467 and PF01247324 caused a concentration-dependent decrease in the C-fiber CAPs in mouse and human vagus nerves. The selectivity of both drugs was tested in NaV1.8 knockout mice. A803467 but not PF01247324 significantly decreased NaV1.8 KO vagal CAPs, indicating that PF01247324's inhibition of wildtype vagal CAPs was solely mediated by NaV1.8, and that A803467 caused inhibition via NaV1.8-mediated and non-NaV1.8-mediated mechanisms. In further studies of wildtype mice, NaV1.8 inhibition following incubation with NaV1.7-selective inhibitor PF05089771 showed no further decrease in mouse vagal CAP, demonstrating that NaV1.8-dependent inhibition affects fibers also sensitive to NaV1.7-dependent inhibition. These data suggest that TTX-sensitive NaV1.7 and TTX-R NaV1.8 cooperate to conduct APs along a select population of vagal nerves. Axonal NaV1.8 inhibition could be utilized to treat aberrant vagal nerve activity in visceral organ diseases.

items.title: Dual C5aR1 and C5aR2 deficiency uncouples neutrophilic inflammation from antibacterial host defense
items.corresponding_institution: Pulmonary Center, Department of Medicine, Boston University Chobanian & Avedisian School of Medicine, Boston, MA, USA
items.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae is a major cause of bacterial pneumonia and mortality worldwide. While host defense critically depends on complement activation, how C5aR1 and C5aR2 orchestrate pulmonary antibacterial immunity remains unclear. We identified alveolar type II epithelial cells as a local source of C5 and confirmed increased susceptibility of C5-deficient mice to infection. Combined C5aR1/C5aR2 deficiency abolished C5a-induced lung inflammation but paradoxically exacerbated neutrophil accumulation during pneumococcal infection, exceeding that observed in either single-receptor deficiency. Despite their abundance, neutrophils exhibited impaired bacterial clearance, excessive extracellular trap formation, accompanied by aggravated lung injury and mortality. CITE-seq revealed profound neutrophil and macrophage dysregulation, identifying distinct neutrophil subclusters with defective antimicrobial programs, increased cell death and altered inflammatory signatures, consistent with functional exhaustion. Thus, C5aR1 and C5aR2 exert complementary, partially non-redundant functions that couple neutrophil recruitment to antimicrobial competence, prevent excessive inflammation, and preserve effective pulmonary host defense.

items.title: An H3K9me3high epigenetic state constrains neuronal activation and synaptic remodeling in the aged dentate gyrus
items.corresponding_institution: Departamento de Neurobiología Celular y Molecular, Instituto de Neurobiología, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM), Querétaro, 76230 México.
items.abstract: How epigenetic states shape neuronal responses to experience and memory remains poorly understood. Here, using a quantitative, single-event approach, our study identifies a subset of neurons that accumulate H3K9me3 (H3K9me3high neurons) via the methyltransferase Suv39h1, specifically in the dorsal dentate gyrus (dDG) of aged mice. FACS coupled to RNA-seq showed that dDG-H3K9me3high neurons express a transcriptional state that fails to induce plasticity machinery despite engaging memory-stabilization programs. Using our novel NucleuSynapse-Tag approach, we found that H3K9me3 accumulation interferes with neuronal activation and synaptic remodeling in response to behavioral stimulation in aged mice. Further, genetically inhibiting Suv39h1 to lower dDG-H3K9me3high numbers improved memory in aged mice. Together, these findings reveal a region- and cell-type-specific epigenetic mechanism linking impaired neuronal responsiveness to age-related memory decline, providing mechanistic insight into the therapeutic potential of targeting Suv39h1.

items.title: Oscillatory Phase Coding Emerges in Adaptive RNNS for Flexible Working Memory
items.abstract: Oscillatory phase coding (OPC) is widely observed in neural systems and has been implicated in cognitive functions such as memory and sequence processing. However, its computational role and neural substrates remain largely unclear. Here, we studied OPC by training recurrent neural networks (RNNs) with adaptation to perform sequence working memory tasks with variable delays. After training, we found that OPC emerges in the RNN spontaneously: the memorized items recur at distinct phases of a shared rhythm, with oscillation amplitude encoding item identity and phase encoding serial order. Ablation studies identified three key elements required for OPC: adaptation in neural dynamics, variable delay in memory retention, and flexibility in reading out information. Neuron-type analysis revealed the emergence of content and time cells in the trained RNN, and they process item identity and sequence order separately. Recurrent connectivity analysis revealed phase-organized connections among time cells and structured connections within digit-selective content-cell groups. Inspired by these findings, we proposed a neural circuit model which reproduces OPC through interactions between content units and an adaptive time ring. Together, this study reveals how OPC arises from network structures and task demands, offers insights into the implementation and computational mechanisms of OPC in biological systems, and inspires us to develop computational models for human-like cognitive functions.

items.title: A GPNMB-associated lysosomal program tracks neurodegeneration across the DAM continuum
items.corresponding_institution: Systems Medicine, Deutsches Zentrum fuer Neurodegenerative Erkrankungen (DZNE), Bonn, Germany
items.abstract: Frontotemporal dementia (FTD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) profoundly remodel microglial states, yet how the heterogeneity of disease-associated microglia (DAM) relates to neurodegeneration remains incompletely understood. Using a progranulin (PGRN) and TMEM106B-deficient mouse model recapitulating key features of frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD), including lysosomal impairment, we demonstrated that CSF1R inhibition reduced microgliosis yet accelerated neurodegeneration, suggesting a protective microglia contribution under lysosomal stress. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed that increasing Gpnmb expression within DAM was associated with a shift from immune and inflammatory processes toward a lysosomal, autolysosomal, and lipid-catabolic program. Across disease models, engagement of the GPNMB-associated program correlated with neurodegeneration. Consistently, A{beta}-driven models with limited neurodegeneration exhibited prominent DAM activation but comparatively limited GPNMB expression and engagement of this program. The GPNMB-associated program was TREM2-dependent, while loss of TREM2 signaling under lysosomal stress was associated with exacerbated neuronal damage. Conversely, lysosomal rescue markedly reduced the GPNMB-associated program, demonstrating its reversibility. CSF proteomics identified a convergent lysosomal and microglial signature across models overlapping with alterations reported in human FTD. Together, GPNMB marks reversible, TREM2-regulated lysosomal transcriptional adaptation along the DAM continuum that scales with lysosomal burden and neurodegenerative severity, consistent with a potentially protective microglial response under lysosomal stress.

items.title: Membrane progesterone receptors spatially organize and partner with ABHD2 to mediate metabolic signaling
items.abstract: Membrane progesterone receptors (mPRs) mediate rapid hormone responses, yet how they engage effectors remains poorly understood. Here, we reveal a spatially regulated partnership between mPRs and the lipid hydrolase ABHD2 that provides a mechanistic basis for the early steps of non-genomic progesterone signaling in mammalian cells. Agonist stimulation promotes mPR-dependent accumulation of predominantly intracellular ABHD2 at the plasma membrane and enhances its association with mPRs. Although human ABHD2 binds progesterone, its phospholipase A2 activity requires partnership with mPRs and an intact catalytic site. ABHD2 deletion disrupts agonist-induced metabolic signaling in hepatic and muscle cells and affects glucose homeostasis in obese mice. Together, these findings uncover a conserved receptor-hydrolase signaling mechanism in which spatially regulated association and receptor-dependent enzymatic activity emerge as defining features of non-genomic steroid signaling.

items.title: Autoinhibition and conformational activation regulate cell-wall anchoring of the bacterial type IV pilus machinery
items.abstract: Type IV pili are widespread bacterial nanomachines that mediate adhesion, motility and host interactions, yet the molecular mechanism coordinating assembly of their outer-membrane channel with attachment to the bacterial cell wall has remained unknown. Here, we show that the conserved PilQ-associated protein TsaP functions as a conformationally regulated envelope adaptor linking secretin assembly to cell-wall anchoring. A crystal structure of full-length TsaP, integrated with structural, biophysical and functional analyses, reveals a compact autoinhibited conformation in which the N-terminal LysM domain is sequestered against the protein core. Comparative structural analyses support a mechanism in which PilQ association remodels TsaP, exposing the LysM domain for peptidoglycan binding. Together, our findings support a mechanistic model in which PilQ-dependent conformational activation of TsaP couples secretin assembly to cell-wall anchoring, providing a framework for understanding the regulated integration of type IV pilus machineries within the bacterial envelope.

items.title: What's in a Story? Studying Neural Narrative Engagement with Auditory Passages Using EEG Inter-Subject Correlation
items.abstract: Narrative engagement - a state implicating attention as well as emotional and sequential processing - is crucial in contexts ranging from social interaction to education. Yet we still lack an understanding of how narrative contents and listener perceptions relate to the neural responses they elicit. In this study, we investigate relationships between auditory narratives and listener responses using electroencephalography inter-subject correlation (EEG-ISC), a measure of neural synchrony that has been shown to correlate with narrative cohesion, attention, preference, and learning. We analyzed dense-array EEG recorded from 46 adult participants who listened to social and non-social narrated literary excerpts. The data were spatially optimized using Reliable Components Analysis, and ISC was calculated for each of the three maximally reliable components (RCs) on a per-stimulus basis. While we found no significant relationships between EEG-ISC and broad social/non-social categorizations of the excerpts, ISC for high sociocognitive word usage significantly exceeded that of medium and low word usage in the third spatial component, RC3. We further observed a significant positive correlation between participants' summed ratings of interest, compulsion, and enjoyment and ISC, both for RC2 and when summed across RC1-RC3. Interaction analyses suggest that passage content and behavioral responses contributed independently as additive effects to these relationships. Taken together, these findings extend previous research utilizing EEG-ISC in natural speech contexts and, importantly, suggest that the decomposition of EEG into maximally correlated spatial components can separate co-occurring neural processes engaged during story listening.

items.title: Intragenic redistribution of RNA polymerase II licenses epigenetic silencing
items.abstract: Co-transcriptional chromatin regulation is widely recognized as a mechanism that reinforces active gene expression, yet transcriptionally active genes must also be able to transition into stable epigenetic silencing during developmental transitions and environmental responses. Whether and how ongoing transcription is coupled to the initiation of epigenetic silencing remains unclear. Here we show that elongating RNA polymerase II phosphorylated at Ser2 (RNAPII-Ser2P) functions as an instructive signal for epigenetic silencing initiation. At actively transcribed genes, RNAPII-Ser2P positions and spatially constrains the FLD-LD H3K4me1 demethylase complex near transcription termination regions, separating the complex from its gene-body H3K4me1 substrate. We found that both chemical perturbation of transcription and physiological silencing cues induce a redistribution of RNAPII-Ser2P into the gene body, accompanied by FLD relocalization and subsequent gene-body H3K4me1 erasure. FLD disengages from chromatin upon gene silencing, indicating that active transcription is required for its continued chromatin association. We further show that LD tethers FLD to RNAPII through an N-terminal HOX domain that binds the C-terminal region of FLD and an adjacent TFIIS domain that contacts the RNAPII CTD in a Ser2P-sensitive manner. This FLD-LD-RNAPII bridge is essential to promote H3K4me1 erasure and gene silencing. Together, these findings reveal a mechanism by which active transcription licenses the initiation of epigenetic silencing.

items.title: Single-cell study of the FCG rat model and cross-species comparison reveal stronger gene regulation by sex chromosome complement in the medial septum
items.abstract: Sex differences are prominent in neuropsychiatric, neurological, and neurodegenerative conditions. While both gonads (ovaries vs. testes) and sex chromosome complement (SCC; XX vs. XY) contribute to sex differences, these effects are hard to differentiate in humans and gonadal contributions have been considered dominant in the brain. The four core genotypes (FCG) mouse model distinguishes between SCC and gonadal effects but whether findings are conserved across species remains unclear. Here, we present the first application of the novel FCG-derived rat model to explore cell-type-specific sex differences in the medial septum (MS), which shows robust structural sex differences, and convergence/divergence between species. Differential gene expression, pathway, transcription factor, and gene regulatory network analyses show dominant SCC effects and concordant gonadal effects on gene and network regulation in rat MS cell types. Comparison between the FCG rat and mouse models find convergence across species on the dominance of the SCC in regulating gene expression in concert with gonadal effects in the MS, despite divergence in individual sex-biased genes. In both species, the sex-biased, cell-type-specific MS genes and networks are associated with diverse diseases relevant to MS functions, such as anxiety, Alzheimers Disease, epilepsy, and schizophrenia, that can be targeted by proposed therapeutic candidates. Our cross-species investigation identifies a conserved dominance of SCC effects in sex-biased gene expression in the MS, thereby challenging the classical gonad-centric view of sexual differentiation in the brain and highlighting the MS as an important region for the study of sex differences driven by the sex chromosome complement.

items.title: Pangenome-guided interpretation of k-mer GWAS inCapsicum
items.abstract: Agronomic trait diversity in Capsicum is shaped by sequence variation that it is not always captured by SNPs called against a single reference genome. Reference-free k-mer GWAS can detect variants beyond SNPs, but significant k-mers are difficult to interpret as they lack genomic coordinates and annotation. In this study, we developed a pangenome-guided workflow to localize significant k-mers in a graph-based Capsicum pangenome. The workflow connects significant k-mers, identified through k-mer GWAS, to genomic positions, their annotations and homology groups. We applied this approach to a metabolite dataset of 343 C. annuum accessions, focusing on the cases of capsaicinoids and specific aroma compounds. For capsaicinoid content, our workflow provided insight in the haplotype composition of the sequenced accessions in the Pun1 locus and the genomic variations contributing to pungency. In the case of dehydroxylinalool oxide, the analysis identified that the haplotype associated to high phenotypes contained an extra terpene synthase (TPS). And last, the production of -ylangene seems to be influenced by a 2 Mb inversion on chromosome 9, right next to a terpene synthase gene. Integrating k-mer GWAS with graph-pangenome localization improves the interpretation of k-mer association signals in complex plant genomes. This workflow can help identify structural variation, haplotypes and candidate loci relevant for trait/metabolic diversity and future breeding applications.

items.title: Combinatorial perturbation structure enables graded inference of signaling activity by CIRCE
items.corresponding_institution: Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research / MIT
items.abstract: Cells decode external inputs into intracellular activities of varying magnitude, and inferring both input identity and strength is crucial for cell-fate engineering. However, perturbation-response models typically treat all cells exposed to a given input as a discrete class, ignoring cell-to-cell variation in response magnitude. Here, we introduce a structured-label framework that infers both input identity and strength from combinatorial perturbation screens without dose-resolved training labels. We represent each perturbation combination in a binary combinatorial space and replace one-hot supervision with a Boltzmann distribution that decays with the Hamming distance between combinations. This approach preserves classification accuracy while improving calibration and resolving continuous pathway activities across individual cells. Importantly, intermediate scores primarily reflect ambiguity in cellular response states rather than insufficient model knowledge. Applied to engineered and natural tissues, the calibrated model successfully recovered graded activities. These results establish combinatorial perturbation screens as a self-calibrating framework for decoding graded cellular responses.

items.title: MDQ: A DockQ-Inspired Scoring Function for Assessing Interface Similarity and Clustering in Molecular Dynamics
items.corresponding_institution: ITODYS, Universite Paris Cite and CNRS, Paris, F-75006 France
items.abstract: Assessing the similarity between protein-protein interfaces is essential for evaluating docking models, yet widely used metrics such as DockQ rely on a single native reference structure and yield asymmetric scores, making them unsuitable for molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories where no reference exists and frame-to-frame comparisons are required. Here, we introduce the MDQ, a fully symmetric reformulation of DockQ designed for MD trajectory analysis. MDQ replaces the fraction of native contacts with the Fraction of Shared Contacts (FSC), and redefines interface and ligand RMSD as weighted variants that penalize low atomic overlap between compared frames. The score can be used to follow structure/contacts convergence of an interface along a trajectory. And it is inverted to produce a true distance metric ranging from 0 (identical interfaces) to 1 (distinct interfaces), directly compatible with distance-based clustering. Applied to two benchmark complexes, Ail-Vitronectin and TGFBR1-FKBP12, MDQ heatmaps reveal global interface stability alongside subtle conformational rearrangements, while DBSCAN and hierarchical clustering of the MDQ distance matrix identifies representative conformational states. Then non-bonding interaction found in clusters were identified by MICLOT software. MDQ thus provides a robust and frame-to-frame symmetric framework for monitoring protein-protein interface conformational and interaction heterogeneity throughout MD simulations.

items.title: TERRA engages MDA5 to shape the immune landscape in ALT brain tumors
items.abstract: In cancer, telomere maintenance is mediated by telomerase reactivation or by the alternative lengthening of telomere (ALT) pathway. Both mechanisms contribute to cancer cell replicative immortality, but ALT, generates telomere instability and promotes inflammation, thus contributing to cancer progression also through non-cell autonomous mechanisms. How ALT telomeres modulate inflammatory signals in cancer is not fully understood, mostly because of the lack of organismal models of ALT+ cancers. Here we used a zebrafish model of ALT+ brain tumor to demonstrate that ALT telomeres promote inflammation through increased transcription of TERRA, which engages RNA-sensing pathways through MDA5. Analysis of ALT+ brain tumors shows that MDA5-MAVS signaling results in the production of interferon responsive genes and cytokines that induce a pro-tumoral immune microenvironment, which can be prevented by abrogating TERRA signaling through in vivo antisense technology, or by CRISPR/Cas9 mediated knock-out of MDA5 or MAVS. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis reveals that abrogating TERRA signaling using ASOs affects both cancer cells and immune cell compartments in a long-lasting manner. These findings reveal a previously unrecognized role of TERRA in modulating immune responses in ALT+ brain tumors and highlight the potential of TERRA-targeting ASOs as a novel therapeutic strategy for ALT tumors.

items.title: Targeting the YAP1/TAZ-TEAD Transcriptional Axis Reveals a Therapeutic Vulnerability in Androgen Receptor Signaling Inhibitor (ARSI)-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.corresponding_institution: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center, New Orleans, LA 70112, USA
items.abstract: Therapeutic resistance remains a major barrier in advanced prostate cancer (PCa), particularly after prolonged treatment with second-generation androgen receptor signaling inhibitors (ARSIs) such as enzalutamide. Tumors can evade these drugs by escaping androgen receptor (AR) dependence through cellular plasticity and lineage transitions, but alternative resistance networks remain poorly understood. Enzalutamide-resistant (ENZ-R) PCa cells showed marked activation and nuclear enrichment of the YAP-1/TAZ-TEAD complex. Disrupting this transcriptional interface with CA3 shows strong anti-metastatic effects, inhibiting migration, invasion, and colony formation across AR-dependent and AR-independent PCa cell lines, suggesting efficacy regardless of cellular lineage or AR status. Similar effects with GNE-7883, K-975, and siRNA knockdown supported a class effect. In vivo, CA3 treatment substantially reduces tumor burden in PC3 and DU145 xenograft models, supporting the systemic efficacy of disrupting the YAP-1/TAZ-TEAD axis in aggressive, AR-independent disease. Mechanistically, this anti-tumor response is driven by potent cytotoxicity: CA3 induces substantial DNA damage and apoptosis in both in vitro and in vivo settings. Moreover, we identified increased YAP-1/WWTR1(Taz) expression as a negative predictor of therapeutic response in PCa patients. These findings indicate that enzalutamide resistance creates a targetable dependence on functional Hippo transcription. Small-molecule disruption of YAP-1/TAZ-TEAD may offer a rational strategy to counter treatment resistance and lineage escape in advanced PCa.

items.title: Retinal Vessel Volume Density and Intraoperative Cortical Vascular Phenotypes in Moyamoya Disease
items.corresponding_institution: Henan Provincial People's Hospital Department of Neurosurgery
items.abstract: Background Angiographic staging describes large-artery stenosis and collateral evolution in moyamoya disease but does not directly depict the cortical surface vasculature, which can vary among patients with similar Suzuki stages. We examined whether a side-matched three-dimensional retinal vascular measure was associated with intraoperative cortical vascular phenotypes after accounting for Suzuki stage. Methods This prospective single-center cohort included 52 patients with moyamoya disease who underwent combined direct and indirect revascularization; 48 had analyzable retinal vessel volume density (RVVD) in the side-matched eye. RVVD was defined as the percentage of the corresponding retinal tissue volume occupied by three-dimensional optical coherence tomography angiography vascular signal within the central 6 x 6-mm region from the retinal nerve fiber layer to the inner plexiform layer. After dural opening and before vascular manipulation, overall cortical vascular richness and arterial, venous, and small-vessel richness were graded from 0 to 3. Associations were evaluated with Spearman correlation and proportional-odds ordinal logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, and ipsilateral Suzuki stage. Results Mean RVVD was 12.92% (SD, 3.30 percentage points). Higher RVVD was associated with greater overall cortical vascular richness ({rho} =0.523; bias-corrected and accelerated bootstrap 95% CI, 0.279-0.714; P<0.001) and arterial richness ({rho} =0.522; 95% CI, 0.261-0.714; P<0.001). Per 1-SD higher RVVD, the adjusted cumulative odds ratio for being in a higher richness category was 3.92 (95% CI, 1.82-8.44; P<0.001) for overall cortical vascular richness and 4.31 (95% CI, 1.92-9.70; P<0.001) for arterial richness. Conclusions In moyamoya disease, higher side-matched RVVD was associated with richer overall and arterial cortical vascular phenotypes at revascularization surgery, independent of Suzuki stage. Three-dimensional retinal vascular imaging may therefore provide a noninvasive, side-specific preoperative measure of cortical vascular remodeling.

items.title: Early locus coeruleus tauopathy features potassium channel dysfunction and is attenuated by Kv7 activation
items.corresponding_institution: Interdisciplinary Research Center on Biology and Chemistry, Shanghai Institute of Organic Chemistry, Chinese Academy of Sciences,Shanghai, China
items.abstract: Background The locus coeruleus (LC) accumulates abnormal tau early in Alzheimer's disease, yet the mechanisms linking early tauopathy to neuronal dysfunction and the potential to modify subsequent pathology remain unclear. We investigated potassium-dependent excitability control, associated molecular 5 changes and Kv7-targeted intervention. Methods We combined electrophysiology, single-cell RNA sequencing, immunohistochemistry and sleep-electroencephalographic recordings in P301S tau transgenic (PS19) mice and wild-type mice receiving local LC inoculation of synthetic human tau fibrils. Pharmacological channel modulation and glycogen synthase kinase- 3 (GSK- 3) inhibition assessed pharmacological modulation of the electrophysiological phenotype. Chronic retigabine treatment assessed pathological outcomes after unilateral locus coeruleus fibril inoculation in young PS19 mice. Results Young, but not aged, PS19 mice exhibited elevated tonic firing and intrinsic excitability of locus 15 coeruleus neurons, associated with pre-tangle phosphorylated tau accumulation and reduced low-threshold potassium current density. Exploratory single-cell profiling identified candidate expression changes in marker-defined noradrenergic neurons: increased stress-associated gene expression coincided with reduced expression of neurofilament, neuronal-maintenance and potassium-channel genes, including Kcnq3 and Kcnd1. Increased nuclear RE-1 silencing 20 transcription factor (REST) and reduced Kv7.2 and Kv7.3 immunoreactivity suggested a candidate transcriptional mechanism associated with channel dysfunction. Local fibril inoculation reproduced the physiological abnormalities in wild-type mice, with hyperexcitability depending on endogenous tau. Combined Kv4/Kv7 modulation attenuated hyperexcitability, while GSK- 3; inhibition reduced tau phosphorylation, increased low-threshold potassium currents and lowered tonic firing. Both models showed increased dark-phase wakefulness and state-dependent electroencephalographic power changes. Chronic treatment with the Kv7 opener retigabine reduced bilateral LC AT8-positive tau burden and was associated with higher tyrosine hydroxylase (TH)-positive neuronal density after unilateral seeding. Conclusions Early LC tauopathy combines impaired potassium channel-dependent excitability control with transcriptional changes consistent with cellular stress and reduced neuronal maintenance. Kv7 activation attenuates seeded tau pathology, supporting excitability regulation as a candidate intervention strategy during early tauopathy.

items.title: Overexpression of α synuclein in Midbrain Dopamine Neurons Drives Learning Deficits in Mice
items.abstract: Parkinson disease (PD) is diagnosed based on core motor features. However, changes in cognitive function are often already present. Cognitive symptoms include changes in executive function, including organization, planning, multi-tasking, and flexible decision-making. These early cognitive deficits have been difficult to model and remain understudied. Here, we investigated whether AAV-based overexpression of wild-type human alpha-synuclein (syn) in midbrain dopaminergic neurons can produce deficits in learning and behavioral flexibility. We found that syn mice develop progressive impairment in basic action-outcome learning. In addition, we found that syn mice show impairments in behavioral flexibility during probabilistic reversal learning. Together, these findings demonstrate that syn overexpression in midbrain dopaminergic neurons is sufficient to drive cognitive decline. Our early-stage PD model offers a temporal window to dissect cellular and circuits mechanisms underlying non-motor manifestations of PD.

items.title: Chronic stress reduces behavioural flexibility and autonomic adaptation when aversive outcomes are controllable
items.abstract: Chronic stress is associated with altered adaptation to threat, yet its effects on aversive learning under varying threat predictability and controllability remain unclear. Thirty participants with chronic stress and thirty healthy controls completed a task to learn how well visual cues predicted upcoming electric shocks (predictability) and whether correct predictions of shocks could reduce shock intensity (controllability). We found that, for controllable conditions, accuracy was similar across varying degrees of predictability in the chronic stress group, whereas accuracy in the healthy control group was highest in highly predictable blocks. The chronic stress group responded more slowly than controls and their skin conductance responses were generally lower and indistinguishable across predictability and controllability. We used a computational model to estimate subjective uncertainty and related these estimates to behavioural responses and skin conductance. Modelling showed that controllability shaped uncertainty differently across groups. In chronic stress, with control, subjective stress reflected uncertainty about likely outcomes, reaction time reflected changing outcome probabilities, and skin conductance reflected unexpected outcomes. Without control, subjective stress reflected unexpected outcomes, reaction time uncertainty about likely outcomes, and skin conductance both unexpected outcomes and outcome uncertainty. In healthy controls, subjective stress reflected changing outcome probabilities with control and outcome uncertainty without control, whereas skin conductance showed the reverse pattern, and reaction time reflected likely outcomes only under control. Together, these findings indicate less adaptation in chronic stress, reflected in reduced modulation of reaction time by controllability and skin conductance by predictability and controllability, alongside altered uncertainty associations across response domains.

items.title: Neural mechanisms of lightness constancy
items.abstract: Object-specific variables are entangled in sensory input. For example, lightness, whether a surface is white or black, not only depends on the surface reflectance but also on the incident illumination. The brain must thus perform inference to achieve a reliable percept of lightness irrespective of illumination (lightness constancy). Whether this results from simple luminance contrast operations early in the visual system or computations at higher levels remains unresolved. We find that neural lightness signals only appear in the extragranular layers of cortical Area V4, and dominate for shadow regions, as opposed to the comparison of local and surrounding luminance (simultaneous contrast). This suggests that lightness is computed downstream from simultaneous contrast, ruling out simple low-level mechanisms, and instead supporting mid-level anchoring theory.

items.title: Microglia and microglia activation are protective in an LSD1-induced model of neurodegeneration
items.abstract: Attempts to determine the function of microglia activation and the immune system in neurodegenerative diseases have yielded conflicting results, with some data showing a protective effect, while other data shows a detrimental effect. This discrepancy in the function of microglia activation and the immune system in neurodegeneration likely stems from differing functions during the build-up of pathological proteins versus later stage defects. Therefore, we investigated the function of microglia activation and the immune system in Lsd1 inducible deletion mice, which serve as a late-stage tau-associated neurodegeneration model without the build-up of pathological proteins. We found that loss of LSD1 causes the morphological and transcriptional activation of microglia, accompanied by astrocyte activation and a broader immune response. Blocking microglia activation by inactivating Trem2 inhibited the entire Lsd1-induced immune response, while pharmacologically inhibiting microglia via PLX3397 treatment eliminated microglia but did not block astrocyte reactivity or the broader immune response. Surprisingly, despite these effects, neither blocking microglia activation nor depleting microglia prevented Lsd1-induced neurodegeneration, paralysis and death. Instead, we found in both cases that survival was significantly reduced.
